The storyline now looks like this: Mariner's Curse ability (Submerge Apprentice Wizard and return to hand) Apprentice Wizard Genesis (Draw a spell) Bottomless Pit ability (Kill Apprentice Wizard since it doesn't have Airborne) And then those three effects will resolve in order, yours first, then mine. See the 'Source is No Longer in the Realm' example below for more details.

links.name: Source is No Longer in the Realm

rule:storyline__simultaneous-effects.title: Simultaneous Effects
rule:storyline__simultaneous-effects.canon: Sometimes multiple effects occur simultaneously, as a single event on the storyline. For example, Windblast involves many cards moving, but they all move simultaneously and are treated as a single event on the Storyline. Simultaneous effects are different from simultaneous triggers. Effects are simultaneous and are resolved as a single event on the storyline if they use language like 'everything.' E.g. Peasant Revolt can simultaneously destroy many cards. An effect is also simultaneous if it uses language like 'each' or 'all,' without also using 'one at a time.' For example, Maelström simultaneously moves many minions and Boneyard simultaneously summons two minions, but Tactical Move is resolved as separate events on the storyline.

rule:storyline__source-is-no-longer-in-t.title: Source is No Longer in the Realm
rule:storyline__source-is-no-longer-in-t.canon: If the source of a storyline event was in the realm but then leaves the realm before the event resolves, the event is ignored and does not actually resolve. Simply proceed to the next event on the storyline. Continuing from the example in 'Multiple Simultaneous Triggers' above, the Apprentice Wizard entered the realm on the surface of a flooded Bottomless Pit with a Mariner's Curse. We have three events on the storyline, as follows: Mariner's Curse ability (Submerge Apprentice Wizard and return to hand) Apprentice Wizard Genesis (Draw a spell) Bottomless Pit ability (Kill Apprentice Wizard since it doesn't have Airborne) The Mariner's Curse resolves, submerging the Apprentice Wizard (who dies underwater without the submerge ability), and the Mariner's Curse returns to your hand. Now, the storyline looks like: DONE: Mariner's Curse ability Apprentice Wizard Genesis (Draw a spell) Bottomless Pit ability (Kill Apprentice Wizard since it doesn't have Airborne) Now, the Apprentice Wizard's Genesis ability tries to resolve, but the Apprentice Wizard is no longer in the realm. The genesis ability cannot resolve and is ignored. I do not draw a spell. Now, the storyline looks like: DONE: Mariner's Curse ability IGNORED: Apprentice Wizard Genesis Bottomless Pit ability (Kill Apprentice Wizard since it doesn't have Airborne) The Bottomless Pit ability resolves. It tries to kill the Apprentice Wizard and fails, since the Apprentice Wizard is already dead. If a specific event has started to resolve and got split up (per the Splitting Events on the Storyline rules), that event will continue to resolve even if the source leaves the realm.

rule:strike.title: Strike
rule:strike.canon: Strike simply means to deal damage equal to the unit's power. For example, if a Bosk Troll strikes, it strikes for 3 damage. In a fight, units strike each other simultaneously. Some abilities allow units to strike first, e.g. Lance. Split power units deal damage equal to their attack power when they strike. Sometimes the striking unit and the unit being struck are at different locations, and some effects (e.g. Mask of Mayhem) care about the location of the strike. For clarity, the strike occurs at the location of the unit being struck.

rule:strike__strikes-vs-multiple-units.title: Strikes vs. Multiple Units
rule:strike__strikes-vs-multiple-units.canon: At the moment a strike is resolving against multiple units, the controller of the striking unit declares how to split up the damage among the struck units. The damage may be split up however you prefer, including assigning zero damage to some units (see below). The total damage assigned must equal the total power of the strike. Units assigned zero damage are still considered struck, and the striking unit makes a total of one strike, split among multiple units. The damage is inflicted simultaneously on all units.

rule:strike__strikes-for-zero-damage.title: Strikes for Zero Damage
rule:strike__strikes-for-zero-damage.canon: A strike for zero damage, e.g. Grandmaster Wizard, is still a strike, even though it doesn't do damage. See the 'zero' codex entry for more details.

rule:strike__multiple-simultaneous-strik.title: Multiple Simultaneous Strikes
rule:strike__multiple-simultaneous-strik.canon: Some effects care about a unit's 'next strike' or 'the next time it strikes.' If the unit is making multiple strikes at the same time (from an effect like Whirling Blades or Leap Attack) then all of those strikes are considered the 'next strike.' This means that a unit with a Lance that is affected by Spin Attack will deal one extra damage on each of it's strikes. Note that this is different from attacking while there are multiple defenders. In that case, the attacker makes a single strike, and the damage is split among the defenders.

rule:stronger-strongest-weaker-weakest.title: Stronger, Strongest, Weaker, Weakest
rule:stronger-strongest-weaker-weakest.canon: Effects with these terms compare the power of two or more units: Stronger: Strictly more power than. Strongest: Strictly the highest power. Weaker: Strictly less power than. Weakest: Strictly the lowest power. In the case of ties for Strongest and Weakest, the active player chooses. When comparing a minion with split power, use the average of their attack power and defense power, rounding down.

rule:submerge.title: Submerge
rule:submerge.canon: Keyword Ability. A minion with Submerge can be summoned to underwater locations and survive underwater. By using one step, a minion with Submerge can move between the surface and subsurface of a water site, or between adjacent underwater locations. A minion with both the Burrowing and Submerge abilities can move directly from an underground location to an underwater location in an adjacent square, and vice versa, in one step. For example, Coral-reef Kelpie can be summoned underwater to one of your water sites. Then, after their summoning sickness wore off, they could use their Move and Attack ability to take a step from underwater to the surface of that site (and that would use up their step). If they were on the surface of a water site, they could use their step to move from the surface to underwater of that site. To 'submerge' means to move from the surface to the underwater of a water site. When an effect 'submerges' a card, you forcefully move that card from the surface to underwater, even if it doesn't have the Submerge ability. If an effect tries to forcefully submerge (e.g. Drown) a card that occupies at least one land site, the effect fails.

rule:subsurface.title: Subsurface
rule:subsurface.canon: The bottom layer of a site. The subsurface of a water site is underwater. The subsurface of a land site is underground. Void squares do not have a subsurface (or surface).

rule:subtypes.title: Subtypes
rule:subtypes.canon: Subtypes provide additional theme and flavor for a card. Subtypes are capitalized and shown in the card's typeline. For example, the card Roaming Monster has the 'Monster' subtype. In general, subtypes have no inherent game effect, but other cards may refer to them. For example, King of the Realm cares about the Mortal subtype. Artifacts have two special subtypes ('Automaton', 'Monument') that do have inherent game rules. See the those codex entries for more details.

rule:summon.title: Summon
rule:summon.canon: Summon means 'enter the realm,' for minions. When you cast a minion spell, the result is that you summon that minion, following normal restrictions about casting spells. When another effect causes you to summon a minion directly without casting it, e.g. Mother Nature, Brother Knight, Knighthood, etc., you simply put it into the realm. You don't need to pay mana, meet threshold requirements, or choose a location you control, as you usually do when you cast a minion spell. Typically a summon effect will specify where the summoned minion appears. For example, Mother Nature specifies that the minion is summoned 'here,' i.e., Mother Nature's location, even if that's an enemy site. If a summon effect does not specify where the summoned minion appears, e.g. Raise Dead or Plague of Frogs, you may summon it to any location in any region. If you try to summon a minion to a location that it can't enter, e.g. Gnome Hollows, it doesn't change zones and remains where it was.

rule:summoning-sickness.title: Summoning Sickness
rule:summoning-sickness.canon: A minion that entered the realm this turn, whether from being cast or from another card's effect, suffers from summoning sickness until the end of turn. A minion suffering from summoning sickness cannot tap, or be tapped, to pay for costs associated with any ability. This includes any additional abilities that may have been granted by spells and artifacts. When you summon a minion on your turn, it enters play untapped, so you may use it to defend on your opponent's turn.

rule:surface.title: Surface
rule:surface.canon: Surface has two meanings in Sorcery! Sorry about that! English is tricky. Surface as a noun means 'the top layer of a site,' as in 'the surface of a site.' This is the more common usage of the word, which you can see on Buried Treasure, Teleport, or Bone Rabble. Surface as a verb means 'to move up from underwater,' as in 'surface the submerged minion.' You can see examples of this on Diluvian Kraken, Iceberg, and Mudflow. Void squares do not have a surface (or subsurface).

rule:tap.title: Tap
rule:tap.canon: Units in the realm can be tapped as a cost to activate various abilities. A player may also need to tap a unit as a cost related to spells or abilities on other cards. A minion with summoning sickness cannot tap or be tapped to pay costs (but may be tapped directly by other effects, e.g. Grievous Insult). To tap a card, turn a it 90° to the right, from an upright position. Only untapped units in the realm can be tapped.

rule:target.title: Target
rule:target.canon: A target is the chosen object of a spell or effect. A spell or effect that targets will and must use the word 'target.' Choosing a target is required. For example, Arc Lightning has a target of a 'nearby unit' and Red Desert has a target of 'nearby site.' The source of the ability, or the caster of the spell, must be in the same region as everything it targets. When you cast a spell or use an ability that targets, before it even goes on the storyline, you must declare all targets. For example, Bury is a spell that targets, and Vile Imp has an ability that targets. You must declare a legal target as the effect goes on the storyline, and the legality of the target is checked again when the effect starts to resolve. If you cannot declare a legal target when the spell or ability would be added to the storyline, the spell isn't actually cast and the ability can't be used. See 'Casting Magics' for more details.

rule:tawny.title: Tawny
rule:tawny.canon: Tawny is a token minion with 1 power. She is a Unique Beast with 'Airborne, Spellcaster, Can't defend.' Tawny is an air minion. See Druid.

rule:teleport.title: Teleport
rule:teleport.canon: Teleportation is forced movement directly from one location to another. Teleportation does not cross borders, and does not have a defined cardinal direction (even if the two locations are in the same row or column). Teleportation can cross regional boundaries unless their effect specifies otherwise. For example, Flanking Maneuver can move minions from one region to another. Blink, however, requires that the unit move to a 'nearby' location, and only locations within the same region are nearby one another. Displace specifies that you move something 'one diagonal step' and steps are always measured within the same region. Teleportation from the same location to itself is not movement at all; in that case, the unit never left the location and never entered it again. See the 'Oversized Units' codex entry for more details on teleportation with oversized units.

rule:the-golden-rule.title: The Golden Rule
rule:the-golden-rule.canon: The Golden Rule of Sorcery is that some text is intentionally informal or necessarily compact. Use common sense and be cool.

rule:the-silver-rule.title: The Silver Rule
rule:the-silver-rule.canon: When card text and rules text conflict, specific card text takes precedence when there is a direct conflict. See also the 'Can vs. Can't' codex entry. The priority from highest to lowest is: Specific card text that says you 'can't' do something. Specific card text that says you 'can' do something. Rules text that says you 'can't' do something. Rules text that says you 'can' do something.

rule:there.title: There
rule:there.canon: 'There' refers to the location(s) that the card occupies. For most cards, such as minions and artifacts, that means one location. For example, Backstab's use of 'there' means the adjacent location of the tapped minion. For auras, that usually means 4 locations, most commonly the surface of 4 sites. For sites, 'there' includes both the site's surface location and it's subsurface location. For example, Upwelling will return subsurface minions and artifacts as well as those on the surface. 'There' is analogous to 'here.'

rule:token.title: Token
rule:token.canon: Token cards are equivalent to normal cards while in the realm. If they would ever leave the realm, they are banished instead. Tokens have a default cost of zero, though if the token is a copy of another card it will copy that card's characteristics. Players may use anything they wish to represent tokens, as long as the game state is clear. The owner of a token is typically whoever put it into play, but if a card is transformed into a token, e.g. Pollimorph or Degradation, the owner of the transformed card is the owner of the token. Typical token minions include: Foot Soldier token Frog token Tawny Bruin Typical token sites include: Rubble Typical token artifacts include: Lance

rule:top.title: Top
rule:top.canon: 'Top' can have two different meanings in Sorcery, depending on context. When referring to your deck, top or topmost simply means the top card of the deck. For example, Mother Nature. When referring to the realm, top means the row farthest from you. For example, Polar Explorers.

rule:top-border.title: Top Border
rule:top-border.canon: The 'top border' of a site is the border farthest from your starting edge. This is relevant for a few cards like Perilous Bridge. 'Top border' is player-relative. If the control of such a card changes, the direction it perceives as 'top border' will also change.

rule:tournament-rules.title: Tournament Rules
rule:tournament-rules.canon: Sorcery is intended to be played in whatever way you and your friends find most enjoyable! If you're attending a tournament, it's wise to be aware of the rules that will apply, ensuring that everyone attending the event understands how it will work. Tournament organizers are empowered to modify the rules to maximize the fun of the players in their community, including banning or modifying cards, modifying the setup rules to provide some compensation for going second, etc. For example, one such setup rule is that after mulligans, the second player may look at the top card of their spellbook or the top card of their atlas, and then may put that card on the bottom. Please check with the tournament organizer of any events you attend to ensure you understand the rules that will be in effect, and most importantly, have fun!

rule:transform.title: Transform
rule:transform.canon: When a card transforms, its printed abilities and characteristics change to match its new form, but it is otherwise the same game object. That means the new form does not 'enter the realm' and does not trigger any 'enter the realm' effects like Genesis - it was there all along! Furthermore, since the new form doesn't enter the realm, it will not suffer from summoning sickness, assuming the old form didn't enter the realm this turn. If one card transforms into a different card, the original card is banished but game effects treat it as the same game object. For example, if you play Pollimorph on my Apprentice Wizard, I end up with a Frog token under my control and the Apprentice Wizard card is banished. If some game effect was tracking the Apprentice Wizard, it is now tracking the Frog token. If one card transforms into a different type, e.g. Island Leviathan, continue to use the same card. When a card transforms, it does not die and deathrites do not trigger. For example, if you Pollimorph my Kettletop Leprechaun into a Frog token, I do not resolve the Leprechaun's deathrite. When a card transform, control of the card does not change unless specified by card text. For example, if I use Descrate on your site, you still will control the new Desecrated Ground. If you summon Mimic to transform one of my artifacts, you will still control your Mimic because of Mimic's specific text, 'under your control.' As mentioned above, the printed abilities and characteristics change to match the new form upon transformation. For example, if a Plumed Pegasus is Shapeshifted into Great Old One, it no longer has Airborne or 3 power, and its Genesis does not trigger. Instead, it has Submerge and 16 power. In contrast, any ongoing effects continue to apply to the new form! For example, if I cast Power of Flight on my Bosk Troll and then I Shapeshift it into Great Old One, it does have Airborne until my next turn, since Power of Flight applies to the game object and isn't a printed ability. The game treats the new form as the same game object. For example, if the old form was tapped, had taken damage, and was carrying an artifact, the new form will also be tapped, have damage, and will be carrying that artifact. Note that Stealth and Ward, though a printed keyword on many cards, are tracked via a Stealth mark and a Ward mark, respectively. Therefore, Stealth and Ward marks will carry over to the new form. For example, if I Shapeshift a Band of Thieves with a Stealth mark into a Great Old One, it will still have the Stealth mark. If I cast Fade on my Bosk Troll and then Shapeshift it into Great Old One, then it will also still have the Stealth mark. Unlike the Airborne example, Stealth and Ward are tracked via a mark, which carries over. Finally, if you Shapeshift a minion into a new form with the printed Stealth or Ward keyword, Stealth and Ward will not trigger since they are an 'enters the realm' effect. You only get the Stealth mark or Ward mark when the minion enters the realm, and it's not entering the realm when transforming.

rule:traverse.title: Traverse
rule:traverse.canon: Traverse means to move through a border. For example, Wall of Brambles specifies that it sits atop a border of a site. Perilous Bridge has a passive ability which affects its top border. To move through a border, a unit must take a step which causes it to enter a location on one side of the border, having occupied a location on the other side of the border.

rule:traverse__on-the-ground.title: On the Ground
rule:traverse__on-the-ground.canon: Some effects use the phrase 'traverse on the ground,' e.g. Wall of Brambles. To 'traverse on the ground,' a unit must move from the surface of a site to the surface of another site, excluding Airborne and Teleportation.

rule:triggered-ability.title: Triggered Ability
rule:triggered-ability.canon: A triggered ability specifies a condition and then an effect. Triggered abilities use words such as 'when,' 'whenever,' and 'at [a specified moment].' For example, Scourge Zombies have a triggered ability. If the act of removing a triggered ability would satisfy its trigger condition, the ability is still triggered. For example: If you play Fields of Phyxis in front of Vindictive Nation, Vindictive Nation will be silenced but its ability will still trigger and cause life loss.

rule:turn-overview.title: Turn Overview
rule:turn-overview.canon: Your turn has three phases: Start phase Main phase End phase

rule:unburrow.title: Unburrow
rule:unburrow.canon: Unburrow means 'to move up from underground.' For example, Mudflow.

rule:uncontrolled.title: Uncontrolled
rule:uncontrolled.canon: Some cards in the realm are uncontrolled, meaning that neither player controls them. For example, a carriable artifact that's not currently being carried is uncontrolled. If an uncontrolled card has a trigger, e.g. Angel's Egg, the owner of the card orders the trigger with other effects they control, as needed.

rule:under.title: Under
rule:under.canon: At the subsurface of a site (not void).

rule:underground.title: Underground
rule:underground.canon: The subsurface of land sites. Whenever a minion without Burrowing occupies an underground location, it immediately dies. An avatar may never enter an underground location. Underground is one of the four regions in the realm.

rule:underwater.title: Underwater
rule:underwater.canon: The subsurface of water sites. Whenever a minion without Submerge occupies an underwater location, it immediately dies. An avatar may never enter an underwater location. Underwater is one of the four regions in the realm.

rule:unit.title: Unit
rule:unit.canon: A unit is a collective term that includes Avatars and minions. Some cards might specify only minions, or only Avatars, but many cards affect units in general.

rule:untap.title: Untap
rule:untap.canon: To untap a card, turn it upright. Even though only units can tap, all of your cards in the realm untap during your Start phase (i.e. if they were previously units and are now no longer units, they still untap).

rule:updated-cards.title: Updated Cards
rule:updated-cards.canon: A few cards have updated rules text that does not match the printed text. These cards have the 'UPDATED:' label on curiosa.io and players should use the updated text. The majority of updates have been made for rules clarity and design intent, often reflecting the way players have been playing these cards all along. See below for the full list. Most Significant Updates Druid - Tawny is only summoned once; the thorns from the flip side only affect your sites; thorns are a site ability, not the Druid's, and thus can be silenced. Druid was very powerful as originally written and repeated summoning of a free minion (i.e. Tawny) limited future design space. Infiltrate - Control of the infiltrated minion returns when it no longer has Stealth, allowing for interesting counterplay. Infiltrate was very powerful as originally written and it was a thematic miss to retain control even after Stealth was lost. Lord of Lies - Don't trust his words, it's in the name! He won't dirty his own hands in the fight any more. Causes two other units to fight. Updates to Match Original Design Intent Daperyll Vampire, Blood Ravens, Sir Galahad, Mask of Mayhem, Grim Guisarme, Lance - The abilities on these cards only work when striking units, not sites. This matches design intent. (In an older version of the rules, units didn't strike sites.) Seirawan Hydra - Hydra can be killed by taking 6 or more damage at once. For example, double defense by two Bosk Trolls will kill a Hydra. This matches design intent and how the card was played for a long time. Deathspeaker - The cast minion is banished; a copy is summoned (using its Genesis) and also banished, matching design intent and avoiding Bottomless Pit shenanigans where the minion could have ended up in the cemetery repeatedly. Mirage - The site you return to your hand must be one you own AND control. This now matches design intent and avoids Desecrate and Heirloom Lost shenanigans where you could steal sites from your opponent. Minor Updates for Clarity Silence, Sisters of Silence, Magnetic Muzzle - These use the 'Silenced' keyword. Heat Ray, Ice Lance, Rhongomyniad - The projectile must actually hit the unit it will damage. Also, these cannot damage the caster. This matches design intent and players were already playing them this way. Askelon Phoenix - The text uses the phrase 'fire damage,' matching design intent and maximizing theme. Vivien the Enchantress - Vivian only copies other abilities. That is, she won't copy abilities from other Viviens, avoiding infinite loops. Pudge Butcher - Pudge can only fight units that actually arrive at his location, matching design intent. Monastery Gargoyle - The Gargoyle turns into a monument so that you retain control of it while it's in artifact form, matching design intent. Purge Juggernaut - The Juggernaut won't kill itself. (In a very old version of the rules, automatons weren't minions!) Squirming Mass - The Mass won't gain its own power while dying, matching design intent. Updraft Ridge - Moving freely away matches design intent. As originally written, the minion would technically lose the movement bonus as soon as it moved away, which wasn't intended. Awakened Mummies - The Mummies fight when they unburrow via their triggered ability. (In an older version of the rules, intercept could interrupt movement.) Torshammar Trinket - The Trinket returns to hand after the turn ends, i.e., after damage has been healed. Also, it will return to hand from the realm even if it's not controlled by anyone. This matches design intent and how players have been playing it. Truesight Crossbow - With truesight, projectiles will hit minions with Stealth, even though hitting with a projectile doesn't target. (In an older version of the rules, Stealth didn't provide protection from projectiles.)

rule:void.title: Void
rule:void.canon: A square without a site is a void. Minions in the void are immediately banished unless they have Voidwalk. Unlike sites that have two locations (surface and subsurface), a void square only has a single location, the void. Voids do not have a surface or subsurface. Avatars in the void have a mandatory action.

rule:voidwalk.title: Voidwalk
rule:voidwalk.canon: Keyword Ability. A minion with Voidwalk can be summoned to void locations and survive in the void. Whenever a minion without Voidwalk occupies a void location, it is immediately banished. An avatar may never enter the void. By using one step, a minion with Voidwalk can move between the surface of a site and the void, the subsurface of a site and the void, or between adjacent void locations. For example, Hounds of Ondaros can be summoned to any void location. Then, after their summoning sickness wore off, they could use their Move and Attack ability to take a step from the void directly to the subsurface of an adjacent site, or directly to the surface of an adjacent site. If they were underground (or underwater or on the surface), they could use their step to move to an adjacent void.

rule:ward.title: Ward
rule:ward.canon: Keyword Ability. If a warded site or unit would be targeted by an opponent's spell or special ability, damaged, or destroyed, the Ward breaks instead. Ward is tracked with a ward mark. A unit or site can have at most one Ward. Evil minions can't be warded. If a Warded minion becomes Evil, remove the Ward mark and they lose Ward. Note that Persecutor only causes your cards to treat the branded minion as Evil, so they keep their Ward mark. Only units and sites can have Wards. If a unit or site with Ward becomes a non-unit, non-site, remove the Ward mark and they lose Ward. A unit or site with the Ward keyword enters the realm with a Ward mark. If a minion or site becomes disabled or silenced, it will lose its Ward mark, since Ward is an ability (similar to Stealth). Further Notes: Ward is a damage prevention effect. For example, if your Daperyll Vampire strikes my warded Apprentice Wizard, the Vampire will try to deal 4 damage, the Ward prevents it and breaks, the Apprentice Wizard survives, and you do not heal from the Vampire's strike. If a warded unit would take damage from multiple sources simultaneously, all simultaneous damage is prevented and the Ward breaks. For example, when a minion with a Ward attacks and multiple units defend that attack. You can target your own warded units and sites with your own spells and special abilities. Ward protects against any damage (from you or your opponent), any destruction (from you or your opponent), and targeting via special abilities and spells (from your opponent only). For example, if I tried to Bury your warded minion, I could cast the magic since your minion is a valid target. The Bury goes onto the Storyline. Then, as Bury resolves from the Storyline, the Ward protects the targeted minion and breaks, and minion isn't burrowed. Ward protects the targeted minion or site at the time the effect resolves. You resolve as much of the effect as you can otherwise. For example, I cast Grievous Insult targeting your warded minion. The spell goes onto the storyline. Then as the Magic is resolving, the Ward protects the targeted minion and breaks, and minion isn't silenced or tapped. Then, I still get to draw a spell. Another example: I cast Bury targeting your warded minion while carrying a Ring of Morrigan. The Bury goes onto the Storyline. The Ring of Morrigan triggers, dealing 1 damage to warded minion. The Ward protects the minion and breaks, dealing no damage. Then, as Bury resolves from the Storyline, the Ward is already gone so the minion is burrowed. A Ward also protects a location at a Warded site from being targeted. At the time the spell or special ability resolves, the Ward will break, and the location will be removed as a target. If a Ward protects a target, additional effects that rely on the target do not resolve. For example, I cast Geyser on your warded site. The Ward protects the site and breaks. No minions gain Airborne, since 'there' references the site, which was the protected target. Similarly, Craterize would deal no damage at all if it targeted a warded site. Another example: My Abaddon Succubus tries to lure your warded minion. The Ward protects the minion and breaks. The protected minion does not take a step closer, does not take 2 damage, and I do not heal 2. Note that Move and Attack is a Basic Ability, and thus Ward does not protect a unit from being attacked. For example, if I have a warded Apprentice Wizard, you can attack it. But, once we get to strikes in the attack sequence, assuming you actually strike for 1 or more damage, the Apprentice Wizard's Ward will break at that point, preventing the damage.

rule:water-site.title: Water Site
rule:water-site.canon: A water site is a site that provides one or more water affinity. If a site provides water affinity and other types of affinity (e.g. earth), it's still a water site (and not a land site). If a site previously provided water affinity and then stops providing water affinity, then it also stops being a water site. 'Land site' and 'water site' are mutually exclusive. A site cannot be both a water site and a land site; it will always be one or the other.

rule:waterbound.title: Waterbound
rule:waterbound.canon: Keyword Ability. This minion is disabled while not occupying at least one water location. The waterbound ability persists even when disabled.

rule:when-it-arrives.title: When it Arrives
rule:when-it-arrives.canon: Some effects use the phrase 'when it arrives.' For example, Grapple Shot. A card 'arrives' when it shares a location with the origin of the effect, after resolving movement, if any. If no movement occurs, but the card shares a location with the origin of the effect, it still 'arrives.'

rule:winning-the-game.title: Winning the Game
rule:winning-the-game.canon: You win the game if you deal a death blow to your opponent's avatar, or if your opponent attempts to draw a card from an empty deck. There may be other effects that cause you to win the game, e.g. Wedding Hall.

rule:wounded.title: Wounded
rule:wounded.canon: A wounded minion is one that has damage (from this turn). A wounded Avatar is one that has current life less than its maximum life.

rule:you.title: You
rule:you.canon: 'You' and 'your' in card text refers to the player. For example, Sparkmage cares about 'spells you've cast,' which includes any spells from any of your spellcasters. As another example, Bone Rabble would trigger if you used your Avatar's ability or if you used Frontier Settlers. Some older cards use the word 'you' to mean 'your avatar.' If it's impossible to read the card as 'player' in a sensible way, then use 'avatar' instead. For example, Cerberus in Chains follows your avatar and Avatar of Earth looks at her own adjacent sites.

rule:zero.title: Zero
rule:zero.canon: In Sorcery, if there is zero of something, the game considers that thing to not exist at all. For example: If a unit takes zero damage, then it did not actually take any damage at all. Triggers looking for damage wouldn't be satisfied. If a unit takes zero steps, then it did not move at all. Triggers looking for movement wouldn't be satisfied. If you draw zero cards, you did not draw any cards at all. Triggers looking for card draws wouldn't be satisfied. etc. There are two notable exceptions: It is possible to strike for zero damage, e.g. Grandmaster Wizard. The unit still made a strike for effects that are looking for strikes (e.g. Phantasmal Shade), but the strike didn't do any damage at all. It's possible for units to have zero power and still exist in the realm. Units with 0 power (e.g. Grandmaster Wizard) only die if they take damage (1 or more). A spell cast for zero mana does not require any mana at all to cast, but it still counts as a cast spell.

rule:zone.title: Zone
rule:zone.canon: A zone is a general area where a card can exist. Game zones include: The realm (a shared zone) Each player's spellbook, atlas, cemetery, collection, and hand zones (specific to each player) The storyline (a shared zone) Additional zones based on specific cards (e.g. Morgana le Fay creates a 'Morgana's hand' zone.) Public zones include the realm and cemeteries, and cards in these zones have no hidden information, i.e. they're face-up, and you're allowed to look at the opposite side of any card in those zones, e.g. Druid. For clarity of game state, it's acceptable to put banished cards face-down in a specific area of the table, but they may be reviewed by either player at any time. The number of cards and type of card (e.g. spell or site) in each zone is public information (e.g. any player can know how many cards remain in any deck, or how many cards of each type you have in your hand). Each player may view the cards in their own hand and collection. Cards in the spellbook and atlas are face-down, and thus not visible to any player.

q.canon: If I target an adjacent enemy already sharing a location with Abaddon Succubus, does it still take 2 damage and heal me 2?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: If the targeted minion takes less than 2 damage (or no damage at all), do I still heal 2?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: Does Abundance apply to my opponent's sites as well?

a.canon: Yes, they will get the benefit as well, if your Abundance affects their sites!

q.canon: When do I get this extra mana?

a.canon: Mana is added to a player's mana pool during their Start Phase, or when a site enters the realm under their control. So, any sites already in play won't get the extra mana until the start of your next turn. But, if you play Abundance and then play a site into Abundance's area of effect, the newly played site will generate extra mana immediately. Also, if you start your turn with a site in Abundance, and then during your Main Phase the site is no longer in Abundance (e.g. Cloud City moving away, Scorched Earth, etc.), you don't lose the mana that you gained during your Start Phase.

q.canon: How much mana is generated by playing an Ordinary Tower (e.g. Lone Tower) into Abundance's effect?

a.canon: 3 mana, because 1 (a site entering the realm under your control) + 1 (Abundance) + 1 (Genesis effect) = 3.

q.canon: Can I choose different squares for the damage?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Is the damage dealt simultaneously?

a.canon: Yes. For example, if you have a 5 power Monster, it will deal 1+1+1+1+1, all simultaneously. If you try dealing it to a warded unit, the Ward will prevent all of it. If your opponent has Shield Maidens nearby, each damage will be reduced. If you have Panpipes of Pnom, it will be 2+2+2+2+2 damage instead.

q.canon: Does this effect kill minions near the Albatross, or near the killer?

a.canon: The minions near the killer die.

q.canon: What does 'cards or allies' mean?

a.canon: Cards in their hand, or allies in the realm.

q.canon: What does 'shuffle if needed' mean?

a.canon: If you searched your spellbook, shuffle it. If you end up summoning the extra Illusionist from your hand or cemetery, you may still have searched your spellbook if you wanted.

q.canon: Does this ability work whenever Adtonitum moves, even if it's my opponent's turn?

a.canon: Yes, this is a triggered ability, which can trigger on your opponent's turn as well, if Adtonitum moves.

q.canon: Can Aino step across the top and bottom edges of the realm if she already has Stealth?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Does this need to be carried to have an effect?

a.canon: Yes, since 'you' or 'your' refers to the controller of the artifact, and carriable artifacts must be carried to be controlled.

q.canon: Must spells cast by the Omphalos match its elements?

a.canon: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

q.canon: Does my avatar still take the damage, but I just don't lose the game?

a.canon: Correct! Damage is still dealt to your avatar for effects that care about dealing damage. You just don't lose the game as a result!

q.canon: When does this artifact provide mana?

a.canon: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller's turn.

q.canon: What does 'can't be targeted or damaged by magic' mean?

a.canon: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

q.canon: Can Magic spells which cause an ally to target a unit (e.g. Shatter Strike) select the bearer of Amulet as the target?

a.canon: Yes, because the ally is doing the targeting, not the Magic spell.

q.canon: If a warded Angel Ascendant fights another minion, the ward will break when the strike happens. So does Angel Ascendant strike for 2 or 3?

a.canon: It will strike for 3 (with the +1 power from Ward). If the opposing minion somehow struck first (perhaps via a Lance), then the ward would indeed break first and then the Angel Ascendant would only strike back for 2.

q.canon: If I cast a Magic as a Spirit minion, will Orb of Ba'al Berith copy it?

a.canon: Good try, but no. You're casting it as a minion, so the game sees it as a Minion spell, not a Magic spell.

q.canon: If I increase or decrease the cost of a magic while I cast it as a Spirit minion, how much power will it have in the realm?

a.canon: Use the printed cost of the magic as its power, regardless of how much mana you actually spent to cast it. Note that magics with X as their cost work appropriately, based on the unmodified cost of the spell when you cast it.

q.canon: If I cast a magic with X as its cost (e.g. Arcane Barrage) as a Spirit minion, will the minion retain the correct power?

a.canon: Yes, because of the golden rule. If you pay 7 mana for your Arcane Barrage Spirit minion, it will have 7 power while in the realm.

q.canon: If Selfsame Simulacrum is summoned as a basic copy of an animated magic, what happens?

a.canon: 'Basic copy' refers to the printed characteristics of the card, which means Selfsame will try to become a magic. But magics cannot exist in the realm, so Selfsame Simulacrum would immediately go to the cemetery and there would be no effect of the magic. Sorry!

q.canon: If I cast a magic as a Spirit minion, do I still get the effect of the magic?

a.canon: No. Treat the textbox of the magic as entirely blank, though it retains its elements and rarity. For example, if you cast Craterize as Spirit minion, you do not need to discard a site as an additional cost, and it will be summoned as an 8 power, Elite earth minion.

q.canon: Can this ability be activated multiple times per turn?

a.canon: Yes, as long as you pay 1 mana for each time you wish to activate it.

q.canon: If I pay to gain water affinity, does this count as a water site this turn?

a.canon: No, activating this ability means the affinity is granted directly to you for the turn, not applied to the site.

q.canon: If there are multiple Apostles of Thamariel in play, do I need to track which Apostles go with which Angels?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: There's a promotional version of this card with the name 'Apurrentice Wizard.' Since it has a different name, does that mean I can have four copies of each in my deck?

a.canon: No, treat 'Apurrentice Wizard' as being named 'Apprentice Wizard' for all deck building and gameplay purposes.

q.canon: When does this artifact provide mana?

a.canon: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller's turn.

q.canon: Do you still need to meet threshold requirements when using its ability?

a.canon: Yes, since you're still casting it (and not summoning it directly).

q.canon: What does 'can't be targeted or damaged by magic' mean?

a.canon: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

q.canon: Does the chosen minion need to have the Spellcaster ability to cast the spell which they draw from this Genesis ability?

a.canon: No, they gain the Spellcaster ability specifically for the purpose of casting that spell. See the rules for 'Only They Can Cast' for specific details.

q.canon: If Michael cannot take a step, does he still get to strike?

a.canon: Yes, but you must declare a legal step if you can, using the normal lookahead rules described in 'Range of Motion.'

q.canon: When I cast one of the banished spells, is that placed back in the cemetery?

a.canon: No. There's no way back from being banished, which overrides the part of resolution that would place the card in the cemetery.

q.canon: When I use the Archimago's ability to banish 3 magic spells and cast 1, do I still have to pay mana and meet threshold?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: When using this ability, must the Archimago be the caster?

a.canon: No, any of your spellcasters can cast the copied spell.

q.canon: What happens if I pay the cost of banishing three spells, but I cannot actually cast any of those three?

a.canon: If you cannot cast any of those three spells, they remain banished and nothing else happens. You did not cast a spell. (If you can cast one of the three, you must.)

q.canon: Can I use this ability to cast Valor or Dodge Roll?

a.canon: No, because the Archimago's ability is an activated ability, which you can only use during your Main Phase when nothing is on the Storyline.

q.canon: If the Army moves through many locations (e.g. Grapple Shot, Seven-league Boots), does it leave many Skeletons behind?

a.canon: Yes! Leave a Skeleton behind each time the Army enters a new location (or takes damage).

q.canon: If an effect grants this free movement (e.g. Arcade of Bones), can I spawn infinite Skeleton tokens?

a.canon: No. Whenever you declare a movement path, you cannot repeat specific steps. Lets say we have sites arranged like this in a row, with Army of the Dead starting on site A, along with an Arcade of Bones: You could declare the following movement path for the Army: A to B B to C C to B B to A None of those steps repeat exactly, so it's all perfectly legal, and you would spawn a Skeleton for each of those steps, for a total of 4 Skeletons spawned. You cannot, however, put another A to B step on the path, since that would be a repeat of the first step.

q.canon: Are the skeletons spawned by this ability summoned? Do they enter the location?

a.canon: Yes! They are summoned, and enter the location where they appear.

q.canon: What is 'fire damage' ?

a.canon: 'Fire damage' is any damage from a fire source, such as a fire minion (including strikes), a fire site, or a fire magic. Morgana le Fay casting Lightning Bolt is not fire damage, since Lightning Bolt is an air spell. Apprentice Wizard casting Firebolts is fire damage because Firebolts is a fire magic (and in fact would be 3 separate instances of fire damage). Anyone casting Grapple Shot that sends a minion into the Phoenix will look at the minion making the strike; if it's a fire minion, it's fire damage. If the Phoenix attacks and there are multiple defenders, each defending fire minion that strikes it counts as a separate source of fire damage.

q.canon: For purposes of cards that care about the mana cost of spells, what is the mana cost of a spell with X?

a.canon: If you cast the spell, the mana cost is X. For example, if you cast it for 2 mana, then Immortal Throne would see it as a 2 cost spell. But, if you aren't casting the spell and it's simply in your hand, spellbook, etc., then X is 0 until you actually cast it.

q.canon: If one of the sites it occupies is an Ordinary water site, are minions and artifacts there still submerged?

a.canon: Yes. It's still affected by the aura, but that effect doesn't do anything to Ordinary sites, other than the Genesis ability.

q.canon: Can you play Rift Valley into an area affected by Atlantean Fate?

a.canon: Yes, since Atlantean Fate only affects the site once it's already in play, and Rift Valley modifies how it's played in the first place.

q.canon: If my Vindictive Nation is affected by my opponent's Atlantean Fate, do they lose 1 or 2 life?

a.canon: Two life. Vindictive Nation is flooded (which counts as modifying it) and then silenced (which also counts as modifying it).

q.canon: What does 'normal size' mean?

a.canon: Anything that occupies exactly 1 location.

q.canon: Does this carry along oversized units or auras that occupy more than one square?

a.canon: No.

q.canon: What does 'your body of water' mean?

a.canon: The body of water (if any) that your Avatar currently occupies. If the Avatar isn't in any body of water, the ability won't function. (They're a fish out of water!)

q.canon: Can you choose an existing water site?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Am I required to summon these units burrowed?

a.canon: Yes. You can and you must.

q.canon: Do they tap when they unburrow?

a.canon: No.

q.canon: Can I target my opponent's minion(s) with Backstab?

a.canon: Yes (but remember the spellcaster must be in the same region as all the targets).

q.canon: If a minion has voidwalk and is in the void, could Backstab move it to an adjacent site to strike a tapped minion there?

a.canon: No. Your spellcaster must target both minions (which are in different regions), but that's impossible since you pick a single location the spellcaster occupies for casting a spell. You can only target minions in the region where the spell is being cast. See 'Casting Spells' for more details.

q.canon: Is the damage resolved one at a time, after each hit?

a.canon: Yes! Resolve the damage (and any deathrites) from the first hit, then bounce for the second hit, resolving that damage, then bounce and resolve the third hit.

q.canon: Can I hit the caster or other allies with this?

a.canon: At the first location of the projectile's path, it cannot hit allies or the caster, even if it hits an enemy there first. If the Ball Lightning leaves the first location, it could bounce back and hit allies or the caster later in its path.

q.canon: After bouncing off a unit, does the ball hit them again immediately since they are both at the same starting location?

a.canon: No. But the ball can hit other units at that location after changing direction, bouncing back and forth.

q.canon: Does this ability damage units at locations in other regions?

a.canon: Yes, one unit at each location in every square in the cardinal direction chosen! This will include surface and subsurface of sites, as well as the void. Beware the evil eye!

q.canon: If I choose to do 2 damage at one location, do I need to do damage at all the locations in that cardinal direction?

a.canon: Yes. If you choose to resolve this effect, you must deal 2 damage to one unit at each other location in the chosen direction.

q.canon: How long does this effect last?

a.canon: When Bane of Aventis' Genesis ability resolves, its controller will gain control of all Warded minions nearby. This change of control is indefinite, and will last even after those minions lose their Wards.

q.canon: If the Battlemage attacks and kills two enemies in a single fight (if my opponent chose to include multiple defenders), does the Battlemage draw two cards?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If the Battlemage activates the 'Move and Attack' ability, doesn't actually attack, and then is intercepted, does that count as 'attacking' the intercepting unit?

a.canon: No. An interception does not cause an 'attack,' and instead is merely a fight between the unit that used 'Move and Attack' and the unit that intercepted.

q.canon: If I declare an attack against one target, but then a different enemy defends, does that satisfy this ability?

a.canon: Yes. An attack was made, and then a minion was killed. As long as your attacking unit used the Move and Attack ability and then got kill credit, this ability is satisfied.

q.canon: If the Battlemage with a Flaming Sword attacks one enemy, and then another enemy dies as a result of the Flaming Sword, does the Battlemage get to draw a card?

a.canon: Yes. An attack was made, and then a minion was killed. As long as your attacking unit used the Move and Attack ability and then got kill credit, this ability triggers.

q.canon: What happens when a minion carries another minion that's carrying a minion?

a.canon: Only the minions you're directly carrying count against your limit. Have fun at the carnival!

q.canon: If my opponent plays an effect that tries to cancel Bedrock in some way (e.g. Atlantean Fate, Smokestacks of Gnaak, etc.), what happens?

a.canon: Bedrock wins, and is not modified in any way.

q.canon: Does this effect target the minion?

a.canon: No! Therefore, the banished minion can be in a different region and/or have Stealth.

q.canon: What happens if the minion stops being Evil while under this effect (e.g. due to Persecutor's Brand wearing off, or Saint of Redemption entering play)?

a.canon: The target only needs to be Evil when the spell is cast and resolves. It will continue to be be disabled, even if it stops being Evil later, until an adjacent Spellcaster taps specifically to release it.

q.canon: What if there was more than one killer last turn?

a.canon: Bitter Departed may teleport to any one of the killers to strike it.

q.canon: How do I resolve this effect?

a.canon: The first eight times the cat would die, it doesn't instead and fully heals. Track its number of lives in some reasonable way. If it gains a deathrite, it does not trigger on the first eight lives, since it doesn't actually die. If the cat is moved to an inhospitable location, e.g. underground or underwater, the game will notice and try to kill it along with any other minions who should die. The other minion's deathrite effects will resolve first, and they'll go to the cemetery. Then the game will notice the cat should die, and continue trying to kill it until it's actually dead and goes to the cemetery.

q.canon: What order are the cards put on the bottom of my spellbook?

a.canon: You choose the order for the cards.

q.canon: Can I reveal fewer than three minions?

a.canon: Yes! You can reveal up to three different Evil minions from the searched spells and draw them.

q.canon: Are these family cards of Castle Servants, Common Cottagers, Blacksmith Family, and Fisherman's Family considered Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spells, respectively?

a.canon: Yes. You can see the spell's colored frame matches those elements, so Castle Servants is an Air spell, Common Cottagers is an Earth spell, Blacksmith Family is a Fire spell, and Fisherman's Family is a Water Spell.

q.canon: How do I resolve this ability?

a.canon: Fully complete the first attack, including deathrites. Then, Bladedancer must take a step to a different location to be able to attack a new unit (or the same unit if it's oversized and occupies multiple locations). The step cannot be intercepted, but the attack is an actual second attack, following the normal attack sequence.

q.canon: How do I resolve this effect?

a.canon: Each minion simultaneously deals 1 damage to its site. Then, starting with the active player and then the non-active player, each minion chooses an artifact at it's location to destroy; you must choose an artifact that hasn't been chosen if possible. Then, all the artifacts are simultaneously destroyed. Finally, all minions tap (and won't untap the next time they normally would).

q.canon: How can I tell if a spell or non-basic ability targets something?

a.canon: It will use the word 'target.'

q.canon: Are random events affected?

a.canon: No. Something like Lightning Bolt ('Deal 3 damage to a random unit at target location') must target Blasted Oak's location, but then the random result is still determined randomly

q.canon: What happens if you have Kythera Mechanism?

a.canon: When you target, you must follow Blasted Oak's restrictions, but you can still choose random outcomes of your choice if you have Kythera Mechanism.

q.canon: Does summoning a minion target the location where it's summoned?

a.canon: No, and therefore Blasted Oak doesn't influence where minions may be summoned.

q.canon: How does this interact with Chain Lightning?

a.canon: You must target all the units you can that share Blasted Oak's site, spending as much mana as needed to do so. Once you've targeted all those units, you could additionally target other units, if you had sufficient mana. For reference, Chain Lightning reads: Deal 2 damage to target unit nearby. Any number of times, you may spend 2 mana to additionally target a new unit nearby the previous one.

q.canon: What is the proper timing of resolution for this effect?

a.canon: If the Blazing unit moves and attacks, the proper sequence is to resolve the move, then deal 2 damage at each departed location simultaneously, then resolve the attack.

q.canon: If the Blazing unit moves over the same location multiple times without stopping, how much damage does Blaze do?

a.canon: Blaze will still only do 2 damage, since a unit is either along the trail, or not. Each time the Blazing unit stops, it creates a separate trail of fire.

q.canon: If the Blazing unit dies, does it deal damage where it died?

a.canon: No. Though it clearly departed its location, it never 'stops,' which is what causes the flame to cause damage. To 'stop,' a unit needs to move first. (Note that if the Blazing unit somehow died while moving, then Blaze would in fact deal damage when the unit died.)

q.canon: Is this magic damage?

a.canon: Yes. The source of the damage is the Blaze spell, not the unit.

q.canon: If a Blazing Megamoeba moves, does Blaze do damage?

a.canon: No, since the Megamoeba still occupies the sites and thus never departed.

q.canon: Does the ally die if it didn't take enough damage from the fights to kill it?

a.canon: No. If the fights with those enemies wouldn't normally kill your ally, your ally will live!

q.canon: Can I cast this on my Avatar when my opponent and I are both on Death's Door to win the game?

a.canon: Yes. Thanks to the golden rule, your avatar will not die until after finishing all of its fights.

q.canon: What is the proper way to resolve the timing for this spell?

a.canon: Choose an ally, then declare an enemy near it to fight, putting that fight on the storyline. Resolve the fight, including any deathrite abilities of the enemy, and place it in the cemetery if it died. Then, repeat the process one fight at a time until the chosen ally has fought all nearby enemies. Finally, if your ally took enough damage, it will now die. That is, you declare and resolve each fight before proceeding to the next one. For example, you play Blaze of Glory on your Autumn Unicorn. I have an Estranged Loner, Muddy Pigs, and my Avatar nearby. You choose to fight my avatar first, so I lose 4 life. Then you choose to fight the Estranged Loner. It dies, I summon a Horrible Hybrids, and the Estranged Loner goes to my cemetery. Then you fight the Horrible Hybrids, it dies too, and goes to my cemetery. Then you fight the Muddy Pigs, they die, I gain 3 life, then they go to my cemetery. Finally, your Unicorn has taken enough damage to die, so it would trigger any deathrite abilities now (if it had any), and then go to your cemetery. A Blaze of Glory indeed!

q.canon: How do I resolve this effect if control of the minion changes between fights (e.g. it had Infiltrate cast on it earlier)?

a.canon: If control of the ally changes in the middle of resolving this effect, the units it sees as 'enemies' will change as well. The caster of Blaze of Glory still chooses the order in which the fights happen. Note that the fights are not optional. For example, I've infiltrated your Autumn Unicorn. You also have a Lugbog Cat and a Skeleton nearby, while I have a Bosk Troll nearby. I cast Blaze of Glory on the Autumn Unicorn. I choose to have it fight your Skeleton first, which breaks stealth, returning control of the Unicorn to you. The Skeleton is removed from the realm. The Unicorn isn't done fighting yet because it still sees an enemy - the Bosk Troll! So the Unicorn fights the Bosk Troll. The Bosk Troll dies and is placed in the cemetery. Then the Unicorn dies and is placed in the cemetery. That is, after each fight, look around and ask 'Are there any nearby enemies I haven't fought yet?' If there is, fight one! Repeat until there are no unfought nearby enemies.

q.canon: Does this need to be carried to have an effect?

a.canon: Yes, since 'you' or 'your' refers to the controller of the artifact, and carriable artifacts must be carried to be controlled.

q.canon: Can a disabled unit Blink?

a.canon: Yes, this is forced movement, not taking a step themselves.

q.canon: The beta foil version of Blink and Blizzard have their title, mana cost, and typeline swapped. Is that a misprint?

a.canon: Yes, this is a misprint. These are not legal for tournament play.

q.canon: The beta foil version of Blink and Blizzard have their title, mana cost, and typeline swapped. Is that a misprint?

a.canon: Yes, this is a misprint. These are not legal for tournament play.

q.canon: Do I still need to meet threshold requirements and pay additional costs, e.g. discarding a site for Craterize?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: How does Blood Mana interact with reduced costs?

a.canon: The same cost you would pay with mana is paid by your life instead.

q.canon: Can I pay more life than I have? What if I'm on death's door?

a.canon: You cannot pay more life than you have. If you're on death's door, you won't be able to pay any life and Blood Mana won't help you.

q.canon: What happens if the next spell I cast is Twist of Fate?

a.canon: Let's say your life is 16 and my life is 20. Therefore, you cast Twist of Fate for 4 mana, but instead of mana, you pay 4 life. Your life is now 12 and the magic goes onto the Storyline. The magic resolves, swapping our life totals. My life is now 12 and your life is 20. Tricky!

q.canon: How do I resolve this effect?

a.canon: You may simultaneously pick up from all adjacent locations. Anything picked up is forcefully moved to the Bogeyman's location. Once it arrives, it is disabled.

q.canon: What happens if the Bogeyman is Silenced or Disabled while carrying enemies?

a.canon: As per the rules about Carrying Units, if the Bogeyman loses his ability to carry enemies, they will be dropped and no longer carried or disabled themselves.

q.canon: What happens if the Bogeyman's power is reduced while carrying enemies?

a.canon: Only check that the enemy is weaker at the time that the Bogeyman targets them with the Pick Up ability. If the Bogeyman loses power or the enemy gains power later, the enemy can still continue to be carried.

q.canon: What is the proper timing of resolution for this effect?

a.canon: Non-active player chooses a minion. Active player chooses a minion. Both minions enter the realm simultaneously. Then, the non-active player resolves any triggered abilities (like genesis), and finally the active player resolves their triggered abilities.

q.canon: If my magic targets my allied minion, does that qualify as 'chooses' for the Book of Blessing?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: If the adjacent site silences the Boulevard (e.g. Smokestacks of Gnaak, Fields of Phyxis), is a Skeleton token is summoned?

a.canon: No. The passive ability from the played site will silence the Boulevard first, before the trigger from Boulevard is checked.

q.canon: If Geomancer creates a Rubble adjacent to Boulevard of Bones, do they create a skeleton?

a.canon: No, the rubble is created in place, not played.

q.canon: How does this effect work?

a.canon: Cards with the printed Mortal type become Beasts, lose the Mortal type, and are silenced.

q.canon: Does the swallowed minion untap? Is it still in the realm? Can it be attacked?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: How does forced movement affect the minion in the Bullfrog's belly?

a.canon: Due to the golden rule, only teleportation-based forced movement effects can move the minion out of the Bullfrog's belly; non-teleportation, forced movement effects can't move the swallowed minion away from the Bullfrog. For example, Blink or Swap would allow the minion to escape, but River Rapids, Riptide, or Scatter would not.

q.canon: What happens if the Bullfrog is disabled or silenced while carrying a minion?

a.canon: The Bullfrog's Genesis ability creates an ongoing effect which allows the Bullfrog to continue to carry a minion in its belly, though it cannot Drop that minion or Pick Up another one. Because this comes from an ongoing effect, the Bullfrog being disabled or silenced will not cause the minion to be dropped.

q.canon: If the swallowed minion is teleported away somehow, does it lose Disabled?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Can the Bullfrog choose to drop the minion it swallowed?

a.canon: No, it can't choose to drop the swallowed minion. (If the swallowed minion is teleported away, it will still be automatically dropped.)

q.canon: How does this effect resolve?

a.canon: 'Access' occurs if a card would leave the collection or cemetery zone, either moving to another zone (i.e. the realm) or being banished. You may still freely look at your collection and cemetery, and add cards to them. The (2) is paid when the ability which would 'access' cards is put on the storyline, allowing the entire effect access. The Bureau does not increase casting costs; it is a separate cost. It will not be reduced by effects that reduce casting cost (e.g. Mix Aer), since it's not a casting cost and often there are effects that access without casting anything (e.g. Adept Illusionist, Imposter, etc.) For example, Archimago must pay (2) to activate his ability, even though 3 cards are banished. Similarly, Deathspeaker must pay (2) to use his ability, even if on Death's Door, as this is not an increase to the cost of the ability but a separate cost which must be paid in advance. You may choose not to pay the (2) and resolve the rest of the effect but be unable to access cards from a cemetery or collection. For example, Feast for Crows may search the other zones and simply not remove any spells from cemetery. Adept Illusionist may search your spellbook and hand for another copy of itself, but not your cemetery.

q.canon: When casting a spell from my cemetery that would banish itself after casting (e.g. Ghostfire), can I choose not to pay the extra cost to keep it from banishing itself?

a.canon: No. You must pay the (2) before even casting the spell, as a separate cost. Once you actually cast it, you resolve the effect normally and your access tax has already been paid.

q.canon: How does the Bureau interact with Wormelow Tump?

a.canon: You still have to pay the Bureau tax! The cards themselves are not being affected; a separate cost is being added to allow you to access them.

q.canon: Do I get the cards immediately when my minion carrying the treasure moves to the surface, even in the middle of something else (like defending or attacking) ?

a.canon: Yes! As soon as your unit is on the surface, you resolve the treasure effect.

q.canon: Do I still need to meet threshold and summoning requirements when I cast the spell?

a.canon: Yes. E.g. It must still be cast to your own site.

q.canon: What does it mean to 'lock' a minion here, and how does the Cage work?

a.canon: All minions with 2 or less power are teleported to the Cage and are carried by it. If the Cage moves, the carried minions move with it. While locked in the cage, the minions remain tapped and disabled. If a minion is somehow no longer carried by the Cage, it is free and no longer disabled. If a minion somehow becomes carried by the Cage (e.g. Swap), it is tapped and disabled.

q.canon: How does forced movement affect minions in the Cage?

a.canon: Due to the golden rule, only teleportation-based forced movement effects can move minions out of the Cage; non-teleportation, forced movement effects can't move the locked minions away from the Cage. For example, Blink or Swap would allow a minion to escape, but River Rapids, Riptide, or Scatter would not.

q.canon: Will this affect minions in the void or underground?

a.canon: No. Because you are looking for adjacent minions, not an adjacent site, you cannot ignore regional boundaries.

q.canon: If these die during my end phase, does their deathrite cause the game to proceed to the next end phase, essentially skipping my opponent's turn?

a.canon: No, when the deathrite resolves during the end phase it does not cause the game to proceed to the next end phase, as you're already in the end phase.

q.canon: If Captain Baldassare attacks a 3 power minion, killing it but also dying in the process, does the Captain have time to use their ability before they die?

a.canon: Yes, by a long shot! In fact, Captain Baldassare's trigger happens as soon as the attack is resolving, even before strikes are made. The trigger for Captain's ability and the Captain dying aren't in the same window of time. The ability triggers first.

q.canon: If Castle Haunt is summoned to a void, e.g. Lucid Dreamers, how does its ability apply?

a.canon: It was never summoned to a site, so it's free to roam around the realm! (Unless it was summoned to The Void site, in which case its restriction applies normally!)

q.canon: If Castle Haunt leaves its summoning site and doesn't immediately die, what happens?

a.canon: It's free to roam around the realm! This could happen because the Castle Haunt is silenced or disabled as soon as it leaves its summoning site, or because it survives via a Ward upon leaving. If it ever returns to its summoning site, its ability will apply again if it tries to leave again.

q.canon: Are these family cards of Castle Servants, Common Cottagers, Blacksmith Family, and Fisherman's Family considered Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spells, respectively?

a.canon: Yes. You can see the spell's colored frame matches those elements, so Castle Servants is an Air spell, Common Cottagers is an Earth spell, Blacksmith Family is a Fire spell, and Fisherman's Family is a Water Spell.

q.canon: What does 'your location' mean?

a.canon: In this case, 'your location' means 'a location that your avatar occupies.'

q.canon: What does 'can't move itself away' mean?

a.canon: Cerberus can't choose to move to a location that is farther from your avatar than its current location. (Count distance using steps that Cerberus would take using its own modes of movement, e.g. Airborne if it gained it somehow.)

q.canon: If your avatar occupies a site you don't control, can you summon Cerberus there?

a.canon: No. The first sentence is an additional restriction on summoning.

q.canon: How does Cerberus in Chains automatically follow you?

a.canon: Whenever your avatar enters a new location, Cerberus in Chains teleports to that location.

q.canon: Do I pay all the costs and choose all the targets when the spell is cast?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Does the damage resolve sequentially or simultaneously?

a.canon: All targets take the damage simultaneously.

q.canon: Can I chain the lightning from target A to target B back to target A?

a.canon: No, that's not what 'new' means. You can only choose new targets that haven't already been targeted by the spell.

q.canon: Can additional targets be in different regions (as long as they're nearby the previous target)?

a.canon: No. Being nearby the previous target is an additional targeting restriction, not a loosening of the targeting rules, so all targets must be in the same region as the caster.

q.canon: Does the minion teleport to the location where it lands?

a.canon: Yes. It teleports to the surface of the site (or void, due to the golden rule) where it lands.

q.canon: What if the minion lands in the void?

a.canon: It deals no damage (even to itself). Since it's now in the void, it is banished (unless it has Voidwalk).

q.canon: What if the minion lands atop two or more sites?

a.canon: It lands on only a single site, which is the one that it most fully overlaps.

q.canon: What if I'm using Chaos Twister on a token? Or a really expensive card with triple sleeves?

a.canon: Feel free to use a stand-in.

q.canon: Does the minion continue to carry whatever it was carrying?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: How should I resolve this card in a tournament setting?

a.canon: This card as-written represents part of our design philosophy for Sorcery. Apply the birthday candle rule, which is that you must blow the card off your hand in a single breath; if you do not, then the effect fails. If the card falls prior to starting to blow, replace it on your hand. Once you start blowing, if the card falls due to anything other than blowing (e.g. hand movement), the effect fails. Call a judge before resolving this card if you're worried, but please be cool and apply the golden rule!

q.canon: What if the minion doesn't land in the grid at all?

a.canon: The teleportation effect doesn't happen and it deals no damage.

q.canon: Where does the copied spell come from?

a.canon: It's a copy, which is a token, so you have unlimited copies, as needed. It doesn't come from your hand or your deck or anywhere else. It's a token!

q.canon: If I have Kythera Mechanism and keep 'randomly' choosing Chaoswish, can I cast infinite spells?

a.canon: Specify the number of times you cast Chaoswish, and then proceed with the game. Your opponent will have the chance to copy Chaoswish that number of times!

q.canon: How do I generate a random spell?

a.canon: Click the button on this page!

q.canon: Once I cast a random spell, how do I track it during the game?

a.canon: Be prepared with index cards + pencil, or some other way to track what gets copied! Note that a copy is a token, so once it leaves the realm, it's banished per normal token rules. Magics (and any other copy) won't end up in the cemetery.

q.canon: What happens if the random spell cannot be cast, e.g. no valid target?

a.canon: The spell is not cast, and the next player may copy Chaoswish.

q.canon: What if the random spell has additional costs, e.g. Craterize?

a.canon: When you cast 'for free,' you don't pay any additional costs. Have fun!

q.canon: Must I choose which of my spellcasters is casting the spell before I know what it is?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: What happens if I play Courtesan Thaïs and then immediately play Chaoswish on the same turn?

a.canon: It's still your turn, so your opponent still controls their own choices. They can freely choose to copy Chaoswish or not. On the other hand, if you cast Courtesan Thaïs first, then on your opponent's turn (which you're controlling) you see that they have Chaoswish in hand and you cast it for them, you can keep copying Chaoswish as long as you want; you will decide for yourself and you will decide for them (since you're controlling their turn).

q.canon: If my opponent and I keep deciding to copy Chaoswish, what happens?

a.canon: You have a lot of fun? In a tournament setting, you'll probably hit the round time limit eventually.

q.canon: Must spells cast by the Omphalos match its elements?

a.canon: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

q.canon: When this is destroyed because it was damaged, who is responsible for the destruction?

a.canon: The source of the damage is responsible, thanks to the golden rule! This will trigger effects like Vindictive Nation, and will be prevented by effects like Order of the Sacred Oak.

q.canon: What happens if the power of one of the units changes during the resolution of this effect so that it's no longer weaker?

a.canon: Only check that the target is weaker when it is initially targeted, and when the effect first starts to resolve from the storyline. Once the effect is resolving and minions are moving, it does not matter if the relative powers change after that point.

q.canon: Is the site played adjacent to the Clay Golem, superseding normal site placement rules?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: Does this carry along oversized minions or auras that occupy more than one square?

a.canon: No. If an oversized minion is now occupying the void, it will be banished. (Megamoeba will still move with Cloud City.)

q.canon: Does this carry along oversized units or auras that occupy more than one square?

a.canon: No.

q.canon: What happens if an oversized avatar is occupying a site, and then some effect moves that site?

a.canon: When a site moves, only things of 'normal' size move with it. As the avatar is now oversized, it will not be moved. In most cases when a site moves, another site will be left in its place (e.g. Rift Valley). In these situations, the avatar will end up occupying the surface of the new site. In the case of Cloud City, which leaves a void location behind, the avatar will now be occupying that void square. See mandatory actions for what happens if your avatar is in the void. Note that in both cases the avatar does not 'enter' the new location that it is occupying.

q.canon: Are these family cards of Castle Servants, Common Cottagers, Blacksmith Family, and Fisherman's Family considered Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spells, respectively?

a.canon: Yes. You can see the spell's colored frame matches those elements, so Castle Servants is an Air spell, Common Cottagers is an Earth spell, Blacksmith Family is a Fire spell, and Fisherman's Family is a Water Spell.

q.canon: Does Cone of Flame extend across multiple regions?

a.canon: No, all affected locations must be in the same region as the caster. By default, the damage grid is restricted to the caster's region. If the caster occupies multiple regions (e.g. a oversized unit), pick a single region where you're casting the spell.

q.canon: All the empty boxes are void and the letters are sites. If the spell is cast from the surface of X, is Z affected?

a.canon: Yes, because it's the same region as the spell effect, even though it's separated by void.

q.canon: If I control Rubble, can my opponent still play a site there?

a.canon: Yes, but it might only feed the worm.

q.canon: Who controls the Consecrated Ground that the site transforms into?

a.canon: Since the site transforms, the controller of the site will not change. Whoever controlled the site that was warded will control the Consecrated Ground. If that site had no controller, no one will control the Consecrated Ground.

q.canon: Does 'has no power here' mean Evil units here have zero power?

a.canon: Yes. Note that when you strike, you determine your power first, then you determine how much damage you deal. So an Evil minion with a Lance would still strike a unit for 1 damage, because it has 0 power and then gets +1 damage from the Lance. See 'Damage' for more details.

q.canon: How do I resolve this effect?

a.canon: Deal face up, one at a time, taking minions from any cemetery. You choose which minions you deal to each site. The dead minions do not actually 'enter' the realm with this effect. Then, damage is dealt simultaneously.

q.canon: Does the type of my minions change everywhere, or just in the realm?

a.canon: Everywhere!

q.canon: Does this ability completely replace their normal type, or simply add a new type?

a.canon: It adds an additional type. For example, your Mortals are Undead and Mortals and would still be silenced by Bower of Bliss. As another example, your Beasts are Monsters and Beasts, so you would still get the discount from a Pond.

q.canon: For Mock Court, Court of Equity, and Mobbed Court, do these effects stack with themselves if multiple copies are in the realm?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: What does it mean for one player to be controlled by another player?

a.canon: If you control a player, you see all their cards and make all decisions for them. You still must make legal choices for them. For example, you still cannot force their minion to move into the void (without Voidwalk) or attack themselves.

q.canon: What happens if there are multiple copies of Courtesan Thaïs played, overlapping each other?

a.canon: The effects can overlap. They do not add additional turns of control beyond what's specified by card text. For example, Turn 1: Player A plays Courtesan 1. Turn 2: Player B is controlled by Player A due to Courtesan 1's effect, and plays Courtesan 2. Turn 3: Player A is controlled by Player B due to Courtesan 1's effect and Courtesan 2's effect. Turn 4: Player B is controlled by Player A due to Courtesan 2's effect.

q.canon: The beta foil version has 1 fire threshold and the normal version has 2 fire threshold. Which is correct?

a.canon: The normal version is correct. You still need 2 fire affinity to cast this minion.

q.canon: What happens if my turn is skipped via Vaults of Zul and Courtesan Thaïs is affecting me?

a.canon: If a turn is skipped then there's no actual turn, which means that part of Courtesan Thaïs's effect would wait for that player's next actual turn.

q.canon: When I control my opponent's turn, can I force them to concede?

a.canon: No. Stop it.

q.canon: Do I still need to meet threshold and summoning requirements when I cast the spell?

a.canon: Yes. It must be cast during your main phase, to your own site, etc. It's an otherwise normal minion spell being cast, except that it's coming from the top of your library instead of your hand, and costs (1) less.

q.canon: Is the ability to look at my top spell a passive abililty?

a.canon: Yes. You may look any time on your turn, including during your Start Phase and End Phase.

q.canon: Do I have to choose 'above' or 'below,' or does it damage both automatically?

a.canon: There is a giant meteor landing in the realm! It damages both above and below - surface, underwater, and underground!

q.canon: All the empty boxes are void and the letters are sites. If the spell is cast from the surface of X, is Z affected?

a.canon: Yes, because it's the same region as the spell effect, even though it's separated by void.

q.canon: Can Crave Golem attack itself?

a.canon: No, per normal attack restrictions (which the Crave Golem respects).
