q.canon: Does it use normal targeting rules when attacking?

a.canon: Yes, except that it may attack other allied minions if they happen to be the chosen target. It still cannot attack Airborne or Stealth units unless it gains a special ability that allows it to do so.

q.canon: How do I properly resolve this ability?

a.canon: First, identify all the minions that Crave Golem can attack within its range of motion. If there are one or more such minions: Randomly pick one, then move (if needed), and attack it. This counts as a normal attack and may be defended. For example, if there's one adjacent minion with Airborne and another without Airborne, it will attack the non-Airborne minion 100% of the time (unless Crave Golem somehow gained Airborne). If there are no such minions: Imagine the Crave Golem had unlimited movement. Are there any minions it could attack now? If not, it doesn't move and the ability is over. If so, take one step toward the minion that requires the fewest Crave Golem steps to reach. (Crave Golem's controller's choice if tied.) This movement cannot be intercepted.

q.canon: Does it tap to take a step or attack?

a.canon: No.

q.canon: When it attacks, does the targeted unit strike back?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: When it attacks, do normal combat rules apply with defending?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If I double twice, is it multiplied by 4?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If I sacrifice Crown Prince (e.g. Moon Clan Werewolf, Cauldron Crones, etc.), does its deathrite still trigger?

a.canon: Yes! When you sacrifice something, it dies, and thus triggers deathrite.

q.canon: The term 'summon' means 'enter the realm.' So, does that mean I can play minions here for free?

a.canon: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon your earth minions.

q.canon: What happens if my opponent plays a site nearby Cursed Land that would silence it (e.g. Fields of Phyxis, Smokestacks of Gnaak)?

a.canon: They will not lose life. This is because Cursed Land's ability is a triggered ability, but Fields of Phyxis and Smokestacks of Gnaak both have passive abilities which apply ongoing effects, and ongoing effects are applied before triggers.

q.canon: Must spells cast by the Omphalos match its elements?

a.canon: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

q.canon: What path can I choose when resolving this ability?

a.canon: See Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic in the Codex.

links.name: Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic

q.canon: What happens if there's no path that can get both the Avatar and the striking unit to the Darkest Dungeon (because of Perilous Bridge, for example)?

a.canon: If there is no legal path that will get both of the involved units to the Dungeon, there will be no movement put on the storyline, and both units will remain where they are.

q.canon: What happens if the ally strikes the avatar during a fight, and is killed by the avatar's strike?

a.canon: If the ally dies as a result of the fight, then you are unable to drag both the ally and the avatar to the Dungeon. The avatar will not move.

q.canon: Can I rotate the cross?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Must the cross be entirely within the realm?

a.canon: Yes. Evil can cower safely in the corners!

q.canon: Does this affect multiple regions, such as the void and subsurface as well?

a.canon: Yes! The card text uses 'affected squares,' which include surface, subsurface, and void.

q.canon: How do I properly resolve the banish and damage effects?

a.canon: Banish Evil minions first, resolving effects (if any) as a result of their banishment. Then, damage all units occupying those six squares.

q.canon: Can I modify the cost of (5)?

a.canon: Yes! If you have Philosopher's Stone and you're playing as Harbinger, you could perhaps cast minions for a mere (3)!

q.canon: Does it kill minions everywhere in the realm, even in the void or underground or underwater?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: At Death's Door, does the Deathspeaker need to meet the threshold requirements?

a.canon: Yes. Only the casting cost is reduced to (0).

q.canon: Can any of my spellcasters cast a spell and still benefit from my avatar's ability?

a.canon: Yes! As long as you control the spellcaster, the game sees it as a spell 'you' cast, meaning the player.

q.canon: When using the Deathspeaker's ability, do I trigger Deathrite effects (perhaps because the minion is on The Geistwood)?

a.canon: Normally no, because Deathrite only triggers when the minion dies, and the Deathspeaker's ability banishes the minion. But, if you somehow kill the minion at the same time it enters the realm (e.g. Bottomless Pit), then Deathrite would trigger. The token dies because of Bottomless Pit (interrupting the Deathspeaker's ability), Deathrite resolves, then the token copy is banished like all tokens when it dies.

q.canon: How does this ability resolve, in detail?

a.canon: You cast the minion spell. Pay mana, meet threshold, banish it from the cemetery, identify where it will be summoned. The minion enters the the realm. (It is a copy of the banished minion.) 'Enter the realm' effects trigger and resolve. These include: Genesis abilities. Effects like Wayfaring Pilgrim, Giant Shark, Mariner's Curse, Bottomless Pit, etc. See 'Simultaneous Triggers' in the Codex for more details. The minion is banished. The intent is that the Deathspeaker can speak to the dead, invoke their abilities, and then release them into the afterlife (whatever that may be). See also 'Splitting Events on the Storyline' and the example with Tawny plus a site's genesis. The Deathspeaker's ability is analogous, since the minion will enter, splitting the Deathspeaker's ability on the Storyline, the genesis ability will resolve (along with any other triggered abilities based on a minion entering the realm), then it will get banished.

q.canon: Can I cast minions from my opponent's cemetery?

a.canon: Yes. You control it when it enters the realm, and then it gets banished.

q.canon: When using the Deathspeaker's ability, do Genesis abilities trigger before the banishing effect?

a.canon: Yes, because events on the storyline are split up when a card enters the realm. See the 'Splitting Events on the Storyline' codex entry for more details.

q.canon: When using the Deathspeaker's ability, are passive abilities applied before the banishing effect? The updated text only mentions Genesis abilities.

a.canon: Yes, the minion is in the realm for a brief moment, so any passive abilities it has will be applied during that window before it is banished.

q.canon: What if my current life is higher than my maximum life after this effect resolves?

a.canon: Your current life is immediately reduced to your maximum life.

q.canon: If an avatar has an odd maximum life, do they round down after halving it?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: What is all of the small text on this card?!

a.canon: Don't tell me you entered into a contract with a Demon without reading the fine print! The smaller text is all of the rules and stipulations for the casting of this spell!

q.canon: What is 'lower' rarity?

a.canon: The order of rarities (from highest to lowest) is: Unique, Elite, Exceptional, and Ordinary. For example, if you control an Exceptional Demon, you could search for an Exceptional or Ordinary spell.

q.canon: Who controls the Desecrated Ground that the site transforms into?

a.canon: Since the site transforms, the controller of the site will not change. Whoever controlled the site that was struck will control the Desecrated Ground. If that site had no controller, no one will control the Desecrated Ground.

q.canon: If I Detonate a minion with the Lethal ability, is the damage from Detonate Lethal?

a.canon: No, the source of the damage is the Detonate spell itself, not the exploding minion.

q.canon: What if I choose a Warded minion to destroy?

a.canon: The Ward breaks instead of the minion being destroyed, but there's still an explosion. After the ward breaks (protecting the minion from the destruction effect), it will still take 3 damage along with the other units at its location.

q.canon: Can you tap minions with summoning sickness for this effect?

a.canon: Yes, it's part of the effect of the spell, not strictly a cost being paid, so you can tap your allies that have summoning sickness for this effect. Note that only untapped units can be tapped, however.

q.canon: Can this teleport a minion or artifact from a site to the void?

a.canon: No. The location the minion or artifact teleports to must be one diagonal step away from where it started, and steps are only measured within the same region. A minion or artifact starting at a surface location can only be teleported to another surface location, for example.

q.canon: Can this teleport an aura from a site to the void?

a.canon: Yes! When moving auras, you ignore the regional boundaries between surface and void locations.

q.canon: Does this count as healing?

a.canon: No, this removes Death's Door and then sets your life to 1.

q.canon: What if I cast this while my life is higher than 1?

a.canon: You set your life to 1.

q.canon: If I break two allied Wards to increase the damage, will it be three instances of 1 damage each, or 3 damage once?

a.canon: Three damage once.

q.canon: If Dodge Roll's mana cost is increased (e.g. Maddening Bells), can you cast it on your opponent's turn?

a.canon: No, because you don't have any mana available on your opponent's turn.

q.canon: If a minion here is attacked what happens?

a.canon: It's not possible to declare an attack against a minion here. If you attack an avatar here and a minion defends, the minion becomes a legal target, per the Defend rules.

q.canon: Does this site protect minions from cards with the word 'attack' in their name, like Leap Attack or Spin Attack?

a.canon: No. Dome of Osiros only prevents 'attacks' from the Move and Attack basic ability, or other card text that uses the word 'attack' (e.g. Crave Golem).

q.canon: When counting 'each unit,' do I include all adjacent squares?

a.canon: Yes! Count any unit in any square adjacent to the summoning square (including the summoning square itself). Each unit counts once, regardless of how many adjacent squares it occupies.

q.canon: When do I choose my set aside Dragon? Can it change during a tournament?

a.canon: You must select your set aside Dragon 'before setup,' which means during deckbuilding. You cannot change it during a tournament. The Dragonlord is loyal to his champion and would not be so fickle!

q.canon: Can my spellbook include a copy of my set aside Unique Dragon?

a.canon: Yes! The set aside Dragon is intended as a rules reference for both players. You may use a suitable substitute for the set aside Dragon, if needed.

q.canon: When the Dragonlord gains the abilities of the set aside Dragon, does the Dragonlord gain its power as well?

a.canon: No, power is a characteristic, not an ability. The Dragonlord will only gain the abilities printed in the text box.

q.canon: Can the Dragonlord gain Stealth?

a.canon: No. Avatars cannot gain Stealth.

q.canon: If the Dragonlord gains Voidwalk, Burrowing, or Submerge, may it enter other regions?

a.canon: No. Avatars cannot enter any region other than the surface.

q.canon: If the Dragonlord gains Ignis Rex's ability, is that considered fire damage? Same question for Adtonitum and air damage?

a.canon: Yes! If the Dragonlord gains Ignis Rex's ability and then discards a fire card, the Dragonlord will deal fire damage. Same answer for Adtonitum and air damage.

q.canon: What does 'attack out of this site' mean?

a.canon: Take exactly one step away from the site, then attack. It doesn't matter if the unit took steps before entering the Dread Thicket, merely that they take exactly one step away from the Thicket and then attack.

q.canon: Does this strike my avatar even if I summon it somewhere else?

a.canon: Yes, Dreadwing will strike your avatar even if they don't share a location when its Genesis resolves.

q.canon: Can I cast this on my Avatar, since they are a spellcaster?

a.canon: Your avatar can't be disabled per their characteristics. Thus, they won't be able to go to sleep, and therefore won't be able to wake up. If you cast this on your Avatar, it will have no effect.

q.canon: Using Dream-Quest, can I put to sleep one of my non-minion Spellcasters (e.g. Omphalos, River of Flame) or a spellcaster with restrictions (e.g. Earl of the Ivory Towers, Wind Sylph)?

a.canon: Yes! An Omphalos will be disabled and thus not draw a spell that turn, but it cannot be hurt unless it's animated. Assuming it is not hurt, you may wake it up at the start of your next turn. For a site (e.g. River of Flame), it provides no Threshold while disabled, but it will wake up in time to produce mana next turn, due to the order of resolution in the Start Phase.

q.canon: How does this ability work?

a.canon: Allies which are nearby to the Marrows, including themselves, can't be forcibly submerged, e.g. Atlantean Fate, Drown, Call of the Sea, etc. Nearby allies can still choose to submerge when taking their own steps via their own submerge ability.

q.canon: Can Floodplain still flood a site affected by Drought?

a.canon: Yes. See 'Example - Flood vs. Drought' in the codex.

q.canon: How do Drought and Flood interact?

a.canon: See 'Example - Flood vs. Drought' in the codex.

q.canon: What is the updated text for the front of the Druid?

a.canon: Tap -> Play or draw a site. If this is your first turn, summon Tawny here. Tap -> Summon Bruin here. Flip this card.

q.canon: Does the Druid's flip side ability work with Poisonous Dagger?

a.canon: No. The site itself gains the ability and is doing the damage.

q.canon: Can the Druid's flip side ability give the Druid kill credit?

a.canon: No. Only units can get kill credit, and the site is source of the damage. The triggered ability is the site's ability, not the Druid's. See the 'kill credit' codex entry for more details.

q.canon: If a site loses its abilities, does the Druid's flip side ability still apply? Can this affect Bedrock?

a.canon: No. The Druid grants an ability to the site. If the site is silenced (or can't be modified in the case of Bedrock), then it loses the ability and will not deal damage.

q.canon: I strike your minion, which is nearby the Drums. Then, you redirect the damage to a bodyguard (e.g. Royal Bodyguard, Sir Gawain), who is not nearby the Drums. Does your bodyguard take lethal damage?

a.canon: No. If the minion actually being damaged is not near the Drums, the damage is not Lethal.

q.canon: How does this ability impact my collection?

a.canon: You may include any cards you wish in your collection, following normal deckbuilding rules. If you have 0 copies of a unique card in your deck, you may include 1 copy in your collection. If you have 2 copies of a unique card in your deck, you cannot include any copies in your collection.

q.canon: If I have Dwarven Digging Team in play, can I choose to summon minions underground without a printed Burrowing ability?

a.canon: No. The units don't gain Burrowing until they're at nearby sites, and you must choose the summoning location when you cast the spell. When you cast the minion spell, it doesn't have burrowing yet, and thus you cannot pick an underground location.

q.canon: What does 'normal size' mean?

a.canon: Anything that occupies exactly 1 location.

q.canon: Does this carry along oversized units or auras that occupy more than one square?

a.canon: No.

q.canon: If the 2x2 area includes some sites and some void, can you rearrange the sites into the void squares?

a.canon: No. You can rearrange sites with other sites as you wish, but the void squares must remain the same.

q.canon: Does diagonal movement include 'sideways' movement?

a.canon: No.

q.canon: What happens if Edge of the World's ability is lost (e.g. Smokestacks of Gnaak), then Edge of the World gets surrounded by sites, then its ability is regained (e.g. Smokestacks of Gnaak moves away)?

a.canon: In this rare case, Edge of the World would destroy itself.

q.canon: What happens if an effect causes edge of the world to not be adjacent to the void?

a.canon: The effect does not resolve. Examples: If you try to move Cloud City to the only void square adjacent to Edge of the World, Cloud City won't move. If you try to play a site from your hand, it won't work and your site will remain in your hand. If you use Earthquake to rearrange sites in a way that Edge of the World isn't adjacent to void, the entire rearrangement fails (and then you still try to burrow.) If you have two Magellan Globes in play at the same location and they're the only thing keeping Edge of the World adjacent to void and they are Dispelled, one is destroyed and other isn't.

q.canon: Turning auras into minions!? Is this real?

a.canon: Yes, indeed. Enchantress is a very versatile Avatar, and one that twists the rules to create very interesting games. Be sure to check these FAQs as well as the auras you're looking to animate. Since many auras occupy a 2x2 area in the realm, you may want to learn about oversized units as well.

q.canon: What is the proper timing of resolution for this effect?

a.canon: Whenever you cast a spell, before that spell resolves, but after targets are specified. See the 'storyline' entry for more details.

q.canon: Can you animate your opponent's auras?

a.canon: Yes, as long as you can target them (i.e. they are in the same region as the Enchantress). Your opponent still controls the aura minion.

q.canon: Can any of my spellcasters cast a spell and still benefit from my avatar's ability?

a.canon: Yes! As long as you control the spellcaster, the game sees it as a spell 'you' cast, meaning the player.

q.canon: Do animated aura change size?

a.canon: No.

q.canon: If Polar Explorers or Ruler of Thul are in play and an oversized unit on the top row moves 'up' one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?

a.canon: This ability only allows movement across the borders, not ongoing occupation. Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied.

q.canon: If Magellan Globe is in play and an Oversized unit on the top row moves 'up' one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?

a.canon: Since Magellan Globe is an ongoing effect that connects the top and bottom edges, the oversized unit can occupy 2 locations on the top row and 2 locations on the bottom row. Ensure that game state is clear, using notes as needed.

q.canon: If Magellan Globe leaves play when a card is spanning the edge of the realm, what happens?

a.canon: Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for a minion, it dies. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for an avatar, shrink it until there is a legal position (Avatar controller's choice), and place it there.

q.canon: Does this affect subsurface units, as well as surface?

a.canon: Yes, since it doesn't say 'atop.' Note that it doesn't affect minions in the void, since the void isn't a site.

q.canon: Do I really have to rip it to pieces?

a.canon: Please see the golden rule! The point is to actually, literally rip the card up, so it will never be playable again. It is banished after you rip it.

q.canon: How does this work in a tournament, especially in best of 1 games, when I rip this?

a.canon: See the rules for that specific tournament, but by default the card is playable. Tournament organizers have latitude to set rules for their events, but one reasonable approach is that you use a deck missing one card for the rest of the tournament (and it's legal to do so).

q.canon: If my opponent gains control of my Erik's Curiosa and then they rip it, who gets to pick the card?

a.canon: They get a card of the controller's choice from the controller's collection (so they get to pick). Hopefully you can still be friends! (They must give you a moment to concede before they rip it.)

q.canon: Does this effect let me break the normal restrictions on deck legality? e.g. duplicate Unique card, or duplicate any site for Pathfinder?

a.canon: The card limits exist only when the game starts; once the game begins, various effects can change your deck composition. So, yes, you are free to get an extra copy of a Unique card via Erik's Curiosa, as long as the card is actually in your collection.

q.canon: How do I resolve this effect?

a.canon: When you would use your avatar's ability (or another ability to play sites without restriction), you may choose to play that site from your collection and banish Ersatz Platz.

q.canon: Must one of my units carry this to gain the mana?

a.canon: Yes! If no one is carrying it, it isn't controlled by you. Without a controller, the Ether Core provides mana to no one. Remember that carriable artifacts must be carried to be controlled!

q.canon: The term 'summon' means 'enter the realm.' So, does that mean I can play minions here for free?

a.canon: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon your minions.

q.canon: Can I summon Evil Twin to a non-surface location if it will be copying a minion that has the appropriate ability (e.g. summon to an underground location while copying a Root Spider)?

a.canon: No. The Evil Twin only gains the abilities as enters the realm, and you must declare its summoning location at the time you cast it, before it enters.

q.canon: What does 'can't be targeted or damaged by magic' mean?

a.canon: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

q.canon: Does this effect count all wards in the realm, or only ones I control?

a.canon: It counts all wards in the realm, on any unit or site!

q.canon: What does 'When the star falls' mean?

a.canon: At the end of each of your turns, during step 1 of the end phase, add a counter to Falling Star. When you add the third counter, you immediately summon a minion and resolve the rest of this effect, then dispel Falling Star.

q.canon: If my summoned minion has a genesis effect, does the genesis resolve before the strike?

a.canon: Yes, resolve the genesis first, including any deathrites. Then, the 'strike each other unit' effect resolves.

q.canon: Are the strikes against other units all simultaneous?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: How does this resolve if I summon an oversized minion?

a.canon: At least one of the summoning sites must include an affected site. The 'strike each other unit where it lands' effect occurs on one affected site of your choice (that the summoned minion occupies).

q.canon: Do I draw a spell if my opponent's minion enters the realm tapped?

a.canon: No. This ability only triggers when a minion goes from being untapped to tapped while nearby the Idol.

q.canon: When you use the ability, what happens to the 'thrown' artifact?

a.canon: It is no longer carried by the Assassin, and is uncontrolled in the target's location. Any unit may pick it up normally (including the Assassin, if it happens to be in that location).

q.canon: Does the Assassin lose Stealth if it uses its ability?

a.canon: Yes. It's an activated special ability, so Stealth is lost per the normal Stealth rules.

q.canon: If I choose a minion that has no Deathrite ability, does it still gain stealth?

a.canon: Yes, it will still gain stealth.

q.canon: What happens if I use this to trigger the Genesis ability of a site my opponent controls?

a.canon: The controller of the site will be the one to resolve the Genesis ability. So in the case of a Desert, your opponent will choose the nearby site where damage is dealt. For a River, your opponent will be the one to look at their next spell and choose to put it on the bottom of their spellbook.

q.canon: Can this be summoned to an inhospitable location (e.g. underground) and die, but still have a chance to use its genesis ability first?

a.canon: No. You cannot choose to summon a minion underground, underwater, or in the void unless it has the appropriate ability.

q.canon: The term 'summon' means 'enter the realm.' So, does that mean I can play this minion for free?

a.canon: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon this minion.

q.canon: What is the proper timing of resolution for this effect?

a.canon: The non-active player chooses a minion, then the active player chooses a minion. Then all other minions are killed. The non-active player resolves any triggered abilities (like deathrite), and finally the active player resolves their triggered abilities.

q.canon: Does the 'adjacent Water site' need to be in the same region as the caster?

a.canon: No. Because the Water site is not targeted, and because the card text uses 'site' instead of 'location,' the site does not need to be in the same region as the caster.

q.canon: Can I cast this spell without a target just to draw a card?

a.canon: No. To cast a spell, you must specify all targets.

q.canon: Does the target need to be in the same region as the caster?

a.canon: No. Normally the answer is yes, but the card text 'above or below' means that normal targeting restrictions are ignored, and the caster can be in any region (surface, underground, underwater, or in the void). As long as there is an adjacent Water site to the caster and a minion occupying that water site, it will get pulled to the caster's location.

q.canon: What does 'one at a time' mean?

a.canon: Resolve the first bolt (including any deathrite or other 'kills' abilities), then resolve the next one, then resolve the 3rd one. Each bolt must go in the same direction.

q.canon: Are these family cards of Castle Servants, Common Cottagers, Blacksmith Family, and Fisherman's Family considered Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spells, respectively?

a.canon: Yes. You can see the spell's colored frame matches those elements, so Castle Servants is an Air spell, Common Cottagers is an Earth spell, Blacksmith Family is a Fire spell, and Fisherman's Family is a Water Spell.

q.canon: If damage is prevented, do I still heal?

a.canon: No. Flagellant must actually take 1 or more damage for you to heal.

q.canon: If Flagellant takes 5 damage, do I heal more than 1?

a.canon: No, just 1. But if Flagellant took 1 damage separately five times, e.g. Abyssal Assault or Arcane Barrage, you would heal 5.

q.canon: What is a 'new site'?

a.canon: A site where this card has not stopped since entering the realm.

q.canon: Does conjuring this into the realm count as 'stopping'?

a.canon: No, something must move in order to stop, and conjuring something into the realm is not movement. To trigger, the Flame has to move from one location to another.

q.canon: Can the grid pattern be flipped horizontally?

a.canon: Yes. You pick the leftmost or rightmost column, and that is where the Flame Wave starts.

q.canon: Can the grid pattern be rotated 90 degrees?

a.canon: No.

q.canon: Is the projectile considered fire damage?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If the attack damage was increased or decreased, does the splash damage include the change?

a.canon: Yes. For example, Critical Strike will splash double damage.

q.canon: If a unit has two Flaming Swords, do they each splash damage?

a.canon: Yes. Have fun dual wielding!

q.canon: Is the splash damage a strike?

a.canon: No. It's damage done by the sword artifact.

q.canon: Does the splash damage occur whenever the unit strikes?

a.canon: Yes. For example, that includes Grapple Shot or other strikes, not just attacks from the Move and Attack basic ability.

q.canon: If the struck unit isn't an enemy, is any damage splashed?

a.canon: No. If there's no 'struck unit,' then it has no location. Also, there are no 'other enemies' when there's no enemy initially. See 'enemy' in the codex.

q.canon: If the Battlemage with a Flaming Sword attacks one enemy, and then another enemy dies as a result of the Flaming Sword, does the Battlemage get to draw a card?

a.canon: Yes. An attack was made, and then a minion was killed. As long as your attacking unit used the Move and Attack ability and then got kill credit, this ability triggers.

q.canon: Do the locations need to be in the same region?

a.canon: No. Teleport effects ignore regional boundaries unless otherwise specified, and the only restriction on this effect is that the locations be a chess knight's move apart on the board. For example, if A is a void square, and B contains a site, Flanking Maneuver can move units from that void location to either the surface or subsurface of the site.

q.canon: How do Drought and Flood interact?

a.canon: See 'Example - Flood vs. Drought' in the codex.

q.canon: Can Floodplain still flood a site affected by Drought?

a.canon: Yes. See 'Example - Flood vs. Drought' in the codex.

q.canon: Can I use Floodplain before Maelström triggers?

a.canon: No. Floodplain is an activated ability, which can only be activated during your Main Phase.

q.canon: Can I cast this onto my opponent's site in an outer column?

a.canon: No, this is an additional casting restriction; it does not allow you to summon Forsaken to locations you normally could not.

q.canon: Can my Free City be struck by opposing units, and if so, will it take damage?

a.canon: Yes, it can be struck, and any strike damage to your Free City will cause your avatar to lose the same amount of life.

q.canon: How do the strikes work?

a.canon: Normally, only units can strike, but card text allows the Free City site to strike as if it were a unit with 3 power.

q.canon: Can Free City die?

a.canon: It's striking as if it were a unit, but it's still a site. Therefore, it won't die due to damage. It can still be destroyed by a specific destruction effect (e.g. Sinkhole), but it won't die due to taking damage.

q.canon: When can it attack?

a.canon: Free City's ability is a passive ability that gives it the option to attack and defend 'normally' once per turn, as if it were a 3 power unit (while actually remaining a site). Therefore, it can only attack on your turn, and defend (presumably on your opponent's turn) when a unit or Free City itself is attacked by an enemy unit occupying Free City. If Free City would somehow have the chance to both attack AND defend on your turn, it can only do one.

q.canon: What can it attack?

a.canon: The key word is 'here.' Clearly burrowed units are 'here.' Airborne and Stealthed units are also 'here.' But, to attack Airborne or Stealth, a unit needs some special ability (e.g. Airborne, Ranged, etc.) Since Free City doesn't have those abilities, it can't actually target Airborne or Stealthed units with an attack.

q.canon: How does the attack work?

a.canon: Since the ability to attack is granted by a card effect and not a basic ability, no tapping is needed, but it's still an attack. Therefore, players may declare defenders for the attack normally.

q.canon: Can Free City attack the turn it enters play?

a.canon: Yes, because only minions are subject to summoning sickness.

q.canon: If an oversized unit occupies Free City while it attacks a different site, can Free City defend against that attack?

a.canon: No, since the attack is not happening on Free City.

q.canon: Can Frontier Settlers play a site that isn't adjacent to your other sites?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If I activate this ability and then move a minion nearby the Horror, does the minion become disabled?

a.canon: No. This ability disables minions that are nearby the Horror when the ability is activated. A minion moving nearby after that moment will not be disabled.

q.canon: Does this affect spells drawn by things like Morgana le Fay and the Omphaloi?

a.canon: Yes. Though those cards end up in another zone, they count as being drawn by the player, and will count against the one spell that can be drawn per turn. For example, if a player draws a site at the start of their turn and then plays Morgana le Fay, Morgana will only draw 1 spell into her hand, resulting in a total of only 1 spell drawn by that player that turn. See the Only It Can Cast entry for more information.

q.canon: Does tapping to free a trapped minion count as interacting with the realm?

a.canon: Yes, tapping to free a minion from its cocoon is activating a special ability, and counts as interacting with the realm.

q.canon: If the minion is not dragged to Gargantula's location, does it still get disabled? What if the minion is already at Gargantula's location?

a.canon: Gargantula must be at the same location as the minion to wrap it in her web, so if the minion cannot be dragged there it will not be disabled. However, if it already shares a location with Gargantula, she will cocoon it.

q.canon: When I play an Earth site using the second ability, do I also place a rubble in an adjacent void?

a.canon: No. You only place a rubble if you play an Earth site using the first ability.

q.canon: When I play an Earth site using the first ability, where does the rubble appear?

a.canon: The rubble must be placed adjacent to your Geomancer. If there's no void adjacent to your Geomancer, then no rubble is placed.

q.canon: Does Mirror Realm (copying an earth site), Valley of Delight (choosing earth), or one of the Bloom sites (i.e. Twilight Bloom) count for Geomancer's first ability?

a.canon: Yes. Mirror Realm works because it applies as it enters the realm. Valley of Delight and the Bloom sites work because the Genesis effect of the site interrupts the resolution of the Geomancer's ability; when the second part of Geomancer's ability actually resolves and looks at the site, the site is indeed an earth (E) site. See 'Splitting Events on the Storyline' for more details on Valley of Delight interaction, analogous to the Tawny example and splitting the Druid's ability.

q.canon: If Geomancer creates a Rubble adjacent to Boulevard of Bones, do they create a skeleton?

a.canon: No, the rubble is created in place, not played.

q.canon: If a unit moves into the site on the same turn, but after Geyser has been cast, does it gain Airborne?

a.canon: No, the minion must be at the site when Geyser resolves to gain Airborne.

q.canon: If I teleport my Ghost Ship from the void to a site, does its ability trigger?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If I summon a Spirit from my opponent's cemetery, do I control it?

a.canon: Yes. (And as usual for an explicit summon effect, you don't need threshold and you don't pay mana.)

q.canon: Will it fight units that are Airborne or Stealthed?

a.canon: Yes. This isn't an attack (which has targeting restrictions), but actually a fight (which simply specifies who fights based on card text).

q.canon: What path can I choose when resolving this ability?

a.canon: See Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic in the Codex.

links.name: Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic

q.canon: Will it fight your own units?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Does 'enters' include minions that are summoned?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If a unit moves within the same site (e.g. surface to underwater, or underwater to surface), does Shark trigger?

a.canon: No, since the unit is not entering or moving between different sites.

q.canon: What happens if I summon my minion with Genesis into my opponent's Shark's body of water?

a.canon: See the storyline codex entry for details.

q.canon: Can the Shark's path include movement from surface to underwater, or underwater to surface, if needed?

a.canon: Yes, as long as the path specified is the fewest steps possible to the target.

q.canon: If a Shark moves through a Silence aura, what happens?

a.canon: The movement and fight still occur. The specific resolution is: Unit enters the water site, Shark's ability triggers. You specify the movement steps to reach the target, and they all go on the Storyline. Shark starts moving. It enters the Silence aura, but the effects of the ability are still on the Storyline and aren't removed, so they continue resolving normally.

q.canon: Do multiple castings of this stack? Does it stack with other abilities that cause the minion's damage to heal me?

a.canon: Yes, each instance of an effect like this will trigger and heal you independently.

q.canon: A minion with Gilded Aegis is on a site chosen for Scorched Earth. The Aegis and the minion are being destroyed simultaneously. Does the Aegis have a chance to save the minion before it's destroyed?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If forcefully burrowed without burrowing, will a unit with Gilded Aegis still die?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Is this effect limited to once per turn?

a.canon: Nope! You may use it as many times as you want in a turn, if you meet the threshold requirement. Of course, in Constructed play, you'll be limited to four, since you can have at most four Horrible Hybrids in your collection.

q.canon: If I have Crusade or House Arn Bannermen affecting my Gnome Hollows, may I summon a 2-power minion there?

a.canon: Yes. It's first summoned (enters the realm), then ongoing effects are applied (e.g. Crusade).

q.canon: If Megamoeba starts at 2 power, can it move into Gnome Hollows (thus getting to 3 power)?

a.canon: Yes. First, Megamoeba enters, then it grows in power immediately after entering.

q.canon: If the most direct path is blocked (Gnome Hollows, Wall of Ice) will the grappling unit move around those obstacles to reach its target?

a.canon: No. 'Dragged' is equivalent to 'Pull,' and 'Pull' requires each location entered to be closer to the destination. Making any detours wouldn't be getting closer to the Avatar, so the unit cannot take that path.

q.canon: How do I resolve this effect?

a.canon: Deal face up to your back row one at a time, placing each card to the surface of a site as you go. Then, shuffle any non-minions and put them on the bottom of your deck. Now all the minions are summoned simultaneously to the location they were dealt to; resolve any effects of those minions being summoned, e.g. genesis effects. Finally, check to see if you're at Death's Door now, and if so, all the summoned minions gain Charge.

q.canon: Can I choose to banish only some minions from the targeted location?

a.canon: No, if you choose to use this ability you must banish all minions at the targeted location with 2 or less power.

q.canon: There's a promotional version of this card with the name 'Grandmeowster Wizard.' Since it has a different name, does that mean I can have two copies of each in my deck?

a.canon: No, treat 'Grandmeowster Wizard' as being named 'Grandmaster Wizard' for all deck building and gameplay purposes.

q.canon: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?

a.canon: The Beta text is correct.

q.canon: Do I resolve all the steps at once, or can effects (e.g. Bottomless Pit) interrupt the movement?

a.canon: See the storyline codex entry for details.

q.canon: Can a disabled unit Grapple Shot?

a.canon: No, since it would be shooting a projectile, and disabled units can't do that.

q.canon: If I Grapple Shot a minion with Submerge through an area affected by Mariner's Curse, what happens?

a.canon: When the Grapple Shot projectile hits the unit, the game adds specific movement steps for the ally to the Storyline: Move A (surface) -> B (surface), Move B (surface) -> C (surface). Then, we start resolving those steps. If Mariner's Curse is on site B, once the unit being dragged reaches site B, it will be submerged, and live. Then the game tries to resolve Move B (surface) -> C (surface), which fails, since the unit isn't on the surface of site B anymore. Thus, there's no strike from Grapple Shot since it didn't reach the hit unit's location.

q.canon: If the most direct path is blocked (Gnome Hollows, Wall of Ice) will the grappling unit move around those obstacles to reach its target?

a.canon: No. 'Dragged' is equivalent to 'Pull,' and 'Pull' requires each location entered to be closer to the destination. Making any detours wouldn't be getting closer to the Avatar, so the unit cannot take that path.

q.canon: Are the minions and artifacts targeted by the allies which drag them down, or by the caster of Grasping Ground?

a.canon: The caster of Grasping Ground must be able to target the minions and artifacts which will be be dragged down by their allies.

q.canon: How does Drought interact with Great Old One?

a.canon: These are both passive effects, so whichever was played last takes precedence.

q.canon: What does it actually mean to permanently flood the realm, including voids?.

a.canon: All sites (including rubble) are flooded for the rest of the game, even sites that enter the realm later.

q.canon: The foil and non-foil beta cards have different text. Which is correct?

a.canon: The non-foil beta text is correct. You may use a foil beta Great Wall in tournament play (or the alpha version), but it must be played with the non-foil beta text; ensure your opponent knows the proper text when it's played.

q.canon: Does this stop all kinds of movement through the top border (e.g. Grapple Shot), or just the Move and Attack basic ability?

a.canon: The Great Wall will stop most kinds of movement on the surface, with a few notable exceptions. Teleportation doesn't cross borders, and if a unit 'moves as if adjacent' (e.g. Waypoint Portal), that also doesn't cross borders. Finally airborne units can fly over the wall as they are not moving 'on the ground.'

q.canon: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?

a.canon: The beta text is correct.

q.canon: How do I resolve this ability?

a.canon: Rasputin must be in your cemetery to use this ability. Then, choose the Evil ally you will banish, which may be anywhere and not limited to your own sites. Since Banishing is the cost of the activated ability, resolve the whole activated ability before actually banishing the minion. (This is analogous to the 'Sacrifice' rules.) Rasputin gains the printed power and abilities of the ally. Resolve Genesis abilities and any 'enter the realm' abilities. Finally, the Banished ally is actually removed from the realm. (Place it under Rasputin as a reminder of the current effect.)

q.canon: Can I banish an evil ally from my cemetery or hand?

a.canon: No, you can only choose an ally in the realm to be banished by Rasputin's ability.

q.canon: How does this ability work?

a.canon: When Reaper kills a minion, the minion is banished instead of dying. In addition, any copies of that minion in play (regardless of who controls them) are also banished. Finally, you search the owner's library of the minion that was killed (and only that player).

q.canon: If a unit is carrying the animated artifact, who retains control?

a.canon: When the artifact is animated, it becomes a minion, and thus cannot be carried. The controller of Grösse Poltergeist gets control.

q.canon: If the unit carrying the animated artifact can also carry minions, who retains control?

a.canon: Grösse Poltergeist says you gain control, but the game rules say that anyone carrying the artifact gains control. Grösse Poltergiest takes precedence due to the golden rule, and the controller of Grösse Poltergeist gets control.

q.canon: Can you 'fly to' a minion already sharing your location?

a.canon: No, that's not 'flying to.' Summon the Guardian Angel to a different location!

q.canon: What path can I choose when resolving this ability?

a.canon: See Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic in the Codex.

links.name: Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic

q.canon: What happens if the power of one of the units changes during the resolution of this effect so that it's no longer weaker?

a.canon: Only check that the target is weaker when it is initially targeted, and when the effect first starts to resolve from the storyline. Once the effect is resolving and minions are moving, it does not matter if the relative powers change after that point.

q.canon: Can it target a unit in a different region?

a.canon: No. Targeting (by default) requires the source and the target to be in the same region.

q.canon: Does the target minion use its enhanced move abilities?

a.canon: Yes. When an effect has a unit 'take steps,' it uses its enhanced move abilities granted by keywords such Voidwalk, Burrowing, Submerge, and Airborne.

q.canon: Does it tap the target minion? Can this movement be intercepted?

a.canon: No and no. This isn't the Move and Attack basic ability, which is what requires tapping and can be intercepted.

q.canon: Consider the group of sites below. An oversized minion occupies 1-2-4-5. Guile Sirens is #5. Can the oversized minion be pulled in any way?

a.canon: Yes. When pulling or pushing an oversized unit, choose a single location the oversized unit occupies (and meets the requirement of the effect), and push/pull from there. So, you could choose Site 2: Oversized minion is pulled South, and ends up at 4-5-7-8. OR, choose Site 4: Oversized minion is pulled East, and ends up at 2-3-5-6. OR, choose Site 5: Oversized minion isn't pulled at all.

q.canon: Is the ability mandatory?

a.canon: Yes. It doesn't use the word 'may.'

q.canon: Does Harbinger's ability combo with other effects that allow you to cast minions, e.g. Elder Ruins, Troubled Town, Peculiar Port, etc.?

a.canon: Yes! It's effectively a passive ability that can be used whenever you cast a spell on your turn. The golden rule, baby!

q.canon: When I determine my three random squares, what if I roll doubles or triples?

a.canon: Reroll any duplicated results until you have three unique squares.

q.canon: When do I determine the random squares?

a.canon: As soon as your Avatar enters the realm, during step 2 of setup.

q.canon: What does 'an ally flies' mean?

a.canon: The chosen unit takes flying steps as if it had the airborne ability. If the unit cannot take steps (due to being immobile, for instance), it cannot move to the targeted minion.

q.canon: What path can I choose when resolving this ability?

a.canon: See Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic in the Codex.

links.name: Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic

q.canon: What happens if the power of one of the units changes during the resolution of this effect so that it's no longer weaker?

a.canon: Only check that the target is weaker when it is initially targeted, and when the effect first starts to resolve from the storyline. Once the effect is resolving and minions are moving, it does not matter if the relative powers change after that point.

q.canon: How does this interact with effects like Browse or Kelp Caverns, which do not say to search, but have you look at cards instead?

a.canon: If the effect does not use the word 'search' in its text, it will not be limited by Haystack.

q.canon: Does this apply if my opponent is searching my deck as well?

a.canon: Yes! Any time your opponent is searching their deck or your deck, they only search the top three cards.

q.canon: What if my Headless Haunt tries to teleport into an illegal location? (e.g. Gnome Hollows)

a.canon: The teleport effect fails, and it remains where it was.

q.canon: What happens to the site that is replaced?

a.canon: The site being replaced is banished.

q.canon: Does this play ability allow me to break normal site placement rules?

a.canon: Yes! You may play this site to replace an Elite or Unique site, even if that site isn't adjacent to your existing sites.

q.canon: Can I attempt to fill the Hemogoblet if it's already full?

a.canon: No, you must empty it first.

q.canon: When hemogoblet is emptied, do I gain mana or life equal to the power of the minion at that moment, or the power of the minion at the time of sacrifice?

a.canon: At the time of sacrifice. Make note of the minion's power when you fill the hemogoblet!

q.canon: What does 'shuffle if needed' mean?

a.canon: If you searched your spellbook, shuffle it. If you end up summoning a beast from your hand, you may still have searched your spellbook if you wanted.

q.canon: If I summon a minion to a location affected by Hillock Basilisk, will my minion's Genesis ability resolve?

a.canon: Yes, the minion will not be at rest until all of its events on the storyline are resolved, including its Genesis ability.

q.canon: If the allied minion was already tapped before using this ability on them, do they still gain Ward?

a.canon: Yes, you resolve as much of this ability as you can. Granting the Ward is not contingent on the minion being untapped beforehand.

q.canon: If my minion gains charge from the Horn to Move and Attack and then leaves the Horn's range, can it finish the attack?

a.canon: Yes, as the minion has already tapped, the rest of the Move and Attack will resolve. Once a charge has been sounded in the heat of battle, there's no stopping it!

q.canon: Does it turn into a Demon minion?

a.canon: Yes, it becomes a minion with the Demon type, and is no longer a site.

q.canon: When it awakens, is it summoning sick?

a.canon: Assuming it was in the realm prior to the turn it awakened, it is not summoning sick (since it was already under your control prior to this turn).

q.canon: Is the ability optional?

a.canon: Yes. It is an activated ability with no cost and a threshold requirement. Like all activated abilities, you can only activate it during your Main Phase when nothing else is happening, but you are not required to activate it.

q.canon: Does it continue to provide fire affinity after it transforms into a Demon?

a.canon: Yes. The transformed Demon provides affinity, due to the golden rule. Obviously, if the Demon dies, you will lose that affinity.

q.canon: What happens if you copy this after it has transformed?

a.canon: Since transform effects permanently change the characteristics of the card, as opposed to temporary modifications of characteristics (i.e. Overpower), the copy effect will take on those new characteristics. For instance, a Selfsame Simulacrum copying an Island Leviathan that has been transformed will enter play as an 8-power Monster minion that provides one water affinity.

q.canon: Does this strike a unit at the location it was summoned to?

a.canon: No, since it will enter that location before its Genesis ability begins to resolve. It will only strike a unit at each of the two new locations it enters while resolving its Genesis.

q.canon: What does it mean to 'permanently lose stealth'?

a.canon: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

q.canon: How do I resolve this effect?

a.canon: Deal face up, one at a time. Then, draw the voidwalk minions and Monsters, and banish the rest. No minions actually 'enter' the realm with this effect.

q.canon: Is the minion only disabled while being carried?

a.canon: Yes, if the minion is no longer carried, it is no longer disabled.

q.canon: What happens if the Hyperparasite is Silenced or Disabled while carrying a minion?

a.canon: As per the rules about Carrying Units, if this loses its ability to carry a minion, that minion is no longer carried, and no longer disabled by this ability.

q.canon: Can this choose to drop the minion it is carrying?

a.canon: Yes, abilities which allow a unit to pick up other units also allow them to drop them.

q.canon: If this stops carrying a minion can it pick up another minion?

a.canon: Yes, it can pick up another minion, or the same minion again.

q.canon: Can this be moved by force while carrying a minion?

a.canon: Yes. It cannot take its own steps while carrying a minion. It can still be moved by force.

q.canon: If Ice Lance doesn't hit anything at the first location where the projectile appears, and then hits something at the 2nd location, how much damage does it do at that 2nd location?

a.canon: 2 damage at the 2nd location. Ice Lance's damage decreases based on locations the projectile enters, not based on how many things it hits or doesn't hit.

q.canon: What is a fire card?

a.canon: Fire sites and fire spells are fire cards. See the 'element' codex entry for more details.

q.canon: What is fire damage?

a.canon: Damage from a fire card.

q.canon: If I play a Village on my opponent's turn via Imperial Road, can I pay 1 mana to summon a Foot Soldier?

a.canon: The genesis effect triggers, but you don't have any mana available on your opponent's turn, so no.

q.canon: Can Imposter wear masks of Avatars with pre-game or setup abilities, and if so, what happens?

a.canon: Yes, you can wear masks of those avatars, and you simply ignore their pre-game or setup abilities since the game has already started by the time you put on the mask. For example: You can use Pathfinder's ability even though your atlas has duplicate sites. You don't get to pick a Unique Dragon as Dragonlord. (Probably not a good choice of masks.) You don't roll for summoning portals as Harbinger. (Probably not a good choice of masks.) Your decks and card sleeves remain as-is for Magician. (Probably not a good choice of masks.)

q.canon: What rarity are Avatars for purposes of including them in my collection?

a.canon: Consider Avatars unique for purposes of including them in your collection.

q.canon: What happens if I impersonate the Druid and then use the ability to flip?

a.canon: You will summon Bruin, flip, ... and then immediately lose the game because you no longer have an Avatar in play! Maybe don't include Druid in your collection?

q.canon: What happens if I impersonate the Realm-Eater, use the ability to destroy a site, and then take damage or otherwise lose that mask before I can digest?

a.canon: The Realm-Eater's ability will have created an ongoing effect which immobilizes you, and can only be removed by activating the 'digest' ability. If you lose that ability, you cannot remove the immobile effect. Be careful!

q.canon: If my Infiltrated unit attacks my opponent's undefended site, do I retain control of it?

a.canon: No. Once the infiltrated minion no longer has stealth, you lose control of it.

q.canon: When does the enemy avatar have the opportunity to pay life?

a.canon: Immediately after the strike, before deathrites resolve. For example, if your strike puts them to 2 or less life, they will not be able to pay 3 life.

q.canon: What happens if I strike for 0 damage?

a.canon: A strike for zero damage is still considered a strike, so it will still trigger Interrogator's ability.

q.canon: Normally pull effects can't cross regional boundaries. Can I actually pull the target minion into the void?

a.canon: Yes, obviously!

q.canon: Can I target a burrowed minion or a voidwalk minion?

a.canon: Not unless you have a burrowed spellcaster or a spellcaster in the void. Since the effect uses the word 'target,' the spellcaster must be in the same region as the target. (There are four regions: surface, underground, underwater, void.)

q.canon: What happens if I target a minion with a Ward when conjuring this?

a.canon: On resolution, the Ward will protect the targeted minion. Due to the Golden Rule, the Ward breaks and the Shackles end up at the same location, not carried.

q.canon: How does this ability work?

a.canon: Any time your Avatar would take damage, you reduce that damage by 2, to a minimum of 0. Note that an enemy striking one of your sites causes life loss to your Avatar, not damage; life loss is not affected by this ability. Each source of damage is reduced by 2. For example, if you attack and three Foot Soldiers defend together, you take 0 damage since each Foot Soldier would do 1 damage, which you reduce. As another example, if you are hit by an Arcane Barrage for 5, you take 0 damage, since each projectile would do 1 damage, which you reduce.

q.canon: Does it turn into a Monster minion?

a.canon: Yes. It becomes a minion with the Monster type, and no longer a site.

q.canon: If the flooded Rubble gets replaced with a site, is the new site also flooded?

a.canon: No.

q.canon: When it awakens, is it summoning sick?

a.canon: Assuming it was in the realm prior to the turn it awakened, it is not summoning sick (since it was already under your control prior to this turn).

q.canon: Is the ability optional?

a.canon: Yes. It is an activated ability with no cost and a threshold requirement. Like all activated abilities, you can only activate it during your Main Phase when nothing else is happening, but you are not required to activate it.

q.canon: Does it continue to provide water affinity after it transforms into a Monster?

a.canon: Yes. The flooded rubble does not provide any affinity to you (since you don't control it), but the Island Leviathan itself does provide affinity, since that's aligned with the golden rule. Obviously if the Monster dies, then you lose that affinity.

q.canon: What happens if you copy this after it has transformed?

a.canon: Since transform effects permanently change the characteristics of the card, as opposed to temporary modifications of characteristics (i.e. Overpower), the copy effect will take on those new characteristics. For instance, a Selfsame Simulacrum copying an Island Leviathan that has been transformed will enter play as an 8-power Monster minion that provides one water affinity.

q.canon: Is Jack the Ripper a Monster as well as a Mortal?

a.canon: Yes! The inclusion of the capitalized 'Monstrous' in his typeline makes him a Monster (and thus Evil).

q.canon: What if the Mortal's location is one where Jack would be silenced? Or disabled?

a.canon: When Jack the Ripper is cast (before he even enters the realm!), his ability is put on the storyline to resolve in the future, when he enters the realm. Silenced upon entering the realm: His ability is already on the storyline, so it still resolves. (A silenced minion can still kill other minions.) He does lose stealth due to silence. Disabled upon entering the realm: His ability is already on the storyline, but when it goes to resolve, he cannot actually kill anyone, since being disabled prevents a minion from taking any actions granted by an effect. He will also lose stealth due to being disabled.

q.canon: Can Jack be cast to a Mortal in a region other than the surface?

a.canon: Yes, but if cast to the void, he will be banished before the rest of his cast ability can resolve. If summoned underground or underwater (or to any location with an effect that would kill him) he will die before he can complete his task as well, assuming he doesn't immediately gain the ability to survive in that location. This means he will neither Silence nor Kill his prey.

q.canon: What if I send Jack the Ripper to commit regicide, casting him to the location of my opponent's King of the Realm?

a.canon: Jack will enter at the King's location and will technically change control briefly to the controller of the King of the Realm, but his ability will already be on the storyline. Jack will then silence and kill the King, and return to your control.

q.canon: The term 'summon' means 'enter the realm.' So, does that mean I can play minions here for free?

a.canon: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon your fire minions.

q.canon: When exactly do the minions fight?

a.canon: After both units have taken their step they will fight from their new locations. If either doesn't move, they haven't passed each other and therefore no joust takes place.

q.canon: How do I 'archive the state of the realm' ?

a.canon: Take a snapshot of the cards in the realm. Players should literally take a picture of it on their phone! If you include this card in your deck, you should be prepared to take a picture during the game. Make additional notes as needed to track things like whether a unit has used its Pick Up and Drop ability for the turn, the controller of a Mesmerized minion, or if there's an ongoing effect on a minion like Power of Flight. Players are expected to make additional notes as needed to be able to recreate the state of those cards, if a picture alone is insufficient.

q.canon: When I 'archive the state of the realm,' does that include players' life totals?

a.canon: No. Players' life totals will not revert when Kairos's deathrite resolves.

q.canon: When I 'archive the state of the realm,' does that include cards outside the realm?

a.canon: No! It does not include any other zone. The thing to focus on are literally the state of cards in the realm right now.

q.canon: Do I archive global effects like Critical Strike?

a.canon: No, since it's not an 'archived card,' but instead an ongoing effect that hasn't yet been applied. The test for inclusion in the archive is if the effect is currently applying to a card in the realm. E.g. Whether or not you've discarded a card for Wizard's Den would be included in the archive.

q.canon: When a card is 'returned to its recorded state,' does it enter the realm?

a.canon: No, it is not entering the realm. Genesis, Stealth, Lance, etc. will not trigger and sites do not generate mana.

q.canon: How do I 'return all archived cards to their recorded state' ?

a.canon: Players should look at the picture they took, then return each card to where it was before, though banished cards can never be returned; sometimes knowledge is truly lost. Once Kairos enters the realm, cards will be tracked across zones solely for the purpose of his deathrite. He's that good of a librarian! If tracking a card across zones is not possible due to hidden information, e.g. shuffled into your deck, then the player may return the card from any zone (but never from banished).

q.canon: When we 'return all archived cards to their recorded state,' do all changes happen simultaneously?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: When a card is 'returned to its recorded state,' does it move or enter the location?

a.canon: No. It does not enter the location; simply place it wherever the picture shows. This is not movement. It's like we're rewinding time, not actually moving cards around.

q.canon: Let's say the realm is archived, then I cast an artifact into my unit's hands, then my unit moves. Then Kairos dies. Does my unit bring its carried artifact when it returns to its recorded state?

a.canon: No! Carried artifacts do move with their bearer whenever their bearer moves, but when you 'return to its recorded state,' that's not considered movement! It's a one-of-a-kind direct placement effect. Therefore, the artifact gets left behind, wherever it is. It's like we're rewinding time, not actually moving cards around.

q.canon: When archived cards are returned to the realm, does that include tokens that were archived?

a.canon: Yes! If a token was in the realm and archived, it will return to its recorded state when Kairos dies. If the token left the realm (and was thus banished), the token still returns to its recorded state, because there are always unlimited copies of tokens available to the players.

q.canon: When we 'return all archived cards to their recorded state,' do all non-archived cards (e.g. cards that entered the realm after Kairos) remain unchanged?

a.canon: Yes. They remain where they are, though if a recently played or moved site is in the way of a site that's returning to its recorded state, the site that's in the way will get banished! See below for more examples and details.

q.canon: When we 'return all archived cards to their recorded state,' what if non-archived sites are in the way?

a.canon: The site that's in the way gets banished! For example, the realm is archived, then Cloud City moves, then a Lone Tower site fills in the square where Cloud City was archived. Then Kairos dies. The Lone Tower is banished and Cloud City returns to its recorded state!

q.canon: What about Earthquake or Rubble?

a.canon: If Kairos archived the realm with Rubble in it, then Rubble will replace whatever sites are there when cards return to their recorded state, banishing any sites in the way! For Earthquake, imagine the following sequence: The realm is archived with sites on squares 3, 8, and 9. Then, a Lone Tower is played on square 4. Earthquake gets played, rearranging sites. Kairos dies. The sites now return to their recorded state. That means the sites that were originally on squares 3, 8, and 9 go back to where they were, all simultaneously. The Lone Tower does not change squares because it was not an archived card. If it's now in the way and in square 3, 8, or 9, it will get banished by the site that's returning there. Don't mess with the Archivist!

q.canon: Can you give a complicated Kairos example?

a.canon: Enjoy this one: I have an Kettletop Leprechaun on Gnome Hollows in square 8. You have a Cloud Spirit on Cloud City in square 3. The realm gets archived. Then: Cloud City moves to square 9 and you summon Bluecap Knockers there. I cast a Grim Guisarme into the hands of my Leprechaun, who moves to square 9. I cast a House Arn Bannerman into the Gnome Hollows. Then, Kairos dies. All of the following happen simultaneously: My Kettletop Leprechaun returns to square 8; even though it's a Gnome Hollows and the Leprechaun has 3 power due to the House Arn Bannerman, remember that the 'return' effect is not movement and is not considered 'entering.' The Grim Guisarme is not an archived card, and it remains where it is on square 9. Carried artifacts move whenever their bearer moves, but returning is not a movement effect, so the artifact doesn't automatically come with the Leprechaun. The Cloud Spirit and Cloud City return to square 3; this is not movement, and thus Bluecap Knockers does not prevent it. The Bluecap Knockers find themselves in the void and are banished. There is a Grim Guisarme in the void on square 9 now. Had there been a site on square 3, it would have been banished as Cloud City returned to that square. When in doubt, always apply the Golden Rule, but especially with Kairos!

q.canon: What if there are multiple Kairos's in play?

a.canon: Whenever a new Kairos archives the realm, that becomes the most recent snapshot for all Kairos deathrite effects. That is, there is only a single archive of the realm at a time. Archivists unite!

q.canon: What if Kairos dies on The Geistwood?

a.canon: Since the deathrite effect and genesis effect will be triggered simultaneously, you may order them as you wish. If you resolve the printed deathrite first, archived cards will return to their recorded state, then the printed genesis effect will not resolve, since Kairos is banished. If you resolve the printed genesis first (as a deathrite due to The Geistwood), the realm will be archived, and then when the printed deathrite resolves, it would return to that very recently archived state, and Kairos would be banished.

q.canon: Can your avatar end up in the void after Kairos dies, and if so, what happens?

a.canon: It's theoretically possible! If it does happen, the mandatory actions rule will apply to you, and if you have a site in hand, you'll be required to play it. The way it could happen is left as an exercise for the reader!

q.canon: Is the state of the Storyline archived? Does the Storyline get restored to its snapshotted state?

a.canon: No! The Storyline isn't archived, and it simply continues to resolve normally after Kairos's deathrite. For example, I have Infernal Legion in the realm on square 8. Then I summon Kairos and the realm is archived. The Infernal Legion moves to square 3, and I summon Vatn Draconis. During my End Phase, I have simultaneous triggers for Infernal Legion and Vatn Draconis. I choose to order the storyline with Vatn Draconis first, then Infernal Legion. So I resolve Vatn Draconis's ability, which kills Kairos. Kairos's deathrite goes on the storyline and resolves before the Infernal Legion ability. When I archived the realm, the storyline was empty. But that doesn't matter because the storyline is different from the realm. We return cards to their recorded state, placing the Infernal Legion back on square 8, and then continue resolving the current storyline, so the Infernal Legion's ability resolves when it's on square 8, even though the ability was added to the storyline when the Legion was on square 3.

q.canon: Units A, B, and C are being attacked; can unit D defend the attack and protect A, B, and C, or just one of them?

a.canon: Just one; you must choose unit A, B, or C to be defended.

q.canon: Units A, B, and C are being attacked; can unit A defend the attack against B, so that B takes no damage?

a.canon: No, since A is already being attacked, they cannot take the Defend reaction.

q.canon: Do each of the attacked units take 6 damage, or is the damage split as the attacker chooses?

a.canon: The damage is split as the attacker chooses.

q.canon: When does this artifact provide mana?

a.canon: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller's turn.

q.canon: How does this ability work?

a.canon: Site abilities cannot target, damage, destroy, banish, modify, move, or impede the movement or attacks of the bearer of the Key. Additionally, site abilities cannot cause the bearer to lose or gain life, and cannot affect healing the bearer receives. For example: Gnome Hollows will not stop a 3+ power Key bearer from entering. A Key bearer can walk over a Perilous Bridge on the ground. Remote Desert will not damage a Key bearer. Poisoned Well cannot cause the bearer to lose life. An Avatar Key bearer will not gain life from Holy Ground or lose life from Poisoned Well. An Avatar Key bearer will not have its healing reduced by River of Blood. (The Avatar itself must hold the Key to ignore the half healing effect from River of Blood.) Fields of Camlann will not destroy a Key bearer, even when it's not the chosen minion. River Rapids can't move a Key bearer. Many site effects won't apply, as part of 'can't be modified': Gilman House can't transform a Key bearer Babbling Brook can't disable a Key bearer Bog can't immobilize a Key bearer Silent Hills can't silence a Key bearer Road to Perdition can't increase or decrease a Key bearer's power Accursed Desert can't break a Key bearer's Ward Some site abilities will continue to work: Wizard's Den will still allow a Key bearer Avatar to draw a spell (since players actually draw spells, not units). Garden of Eden will still stop a Key bearer Avatar from drawing extra spells (since players actually draw spells, not units). Beacon will still count an enemy Key bearer. Asmodeus with the Key still can't destroy a Bedrock. A Key bearer Avatar will still have to pay (2) extra for Bureau of Occult Control, since gaining and paying mana is done by the player. A Key bearer Avatar will still be able to use the threshold provided by The Empyrean's site ability, since tracking threshold is done by the player. The Void site would still banish a non-voidwalk minion Key bearer, since the game itself is banishing the minion.

q.canon: How does this ability interact with Flooded sites?

a.canon: The Flooded ability gives a site a minimum of 1 water threshold, making it a water site. Even a bearer of Key to the City will see the water threshold and treat it as a water site. e.g. It will die in the subsurface if it doesn't have Submerge, it can't be forcefully Burrowed, etc.

q.canon: What happens if I use this to trigger the Genesis ability of a site my opponent controls?

a.canon: The controller of the site will be the one to resolve the Genesis ability. So in the case of a Desert, your opponent will choose the nearby site where damage is dealt. For a River, your opponent will be the one to look at their next spell and choose to put it on the bottom of their spellbook.

q.canon: What happens if King Arthur is in the realm and my opponent would control a card I own?

a.canon: While King Arthur rules the realm, if your opponent would control a card you own, you control it instead (applying equally for both players). For example: My opponent plays Lilith then summons a minion from my deck. My opponent would normally control a minion they summoned, but I control it while King Arthur is in the realm. I play Heirloom Lost, Postern Gate, Desecrate to get a Desecrated Ground, etc. My opponent would normally control that site I own, but I control the site while King Arthur is in the realm. I play any Relic (e.g. Ring of Morrigan) and my opponent takes it somehow (e.g. Swap). My opponent would normally control that relic while carrying it, but I control it while King Arthur is in the realm. Even if I control it, my opponent's unit is still the bearer and can benefit from bearer abilities. Since I control it, terms like 'ally' and 'enemy' apply from my perspective (the controller). If it's dropped, no one controls it, as normal. I animate my aura via Enchantress. You play Mesmerism on it. Even after it returns to being a normal aura, you would normally control it, but I control it while King Arthur is in the realm.

q.canon: How does the Philosopher's Stone work with multi-element cards, such as King Arthur and Queen Guienevere? Would King Arthur, who requires 4 mana, cost 3 or 0 Mana to cast using the Stone?

a.canon:
Cards that have different element symbols count as a spell of each of those affinities. So Arthur and Guinevere are each an Air spell, an Earth spell, a Fire spell, and a Water spell, all at the same time. But you are still casting them together as a single spell. So, assuming Arthur is your spellcaster's first spell of the turn, the Stone will offer a discount of 1 mana for Arthur, making him cost 3 mana.
This also means that when Arthur is played he uses up the Stone for that spellcaster's turn because he's simultaneously the first Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spell played this turn. So the Spellcaster cannot continue to use the stone that turn.

q.canon: What Mortals are affected by the first ability?

a.canon: All Mortals, anywhere in the realm.

q.canon: If a Mortal with Deathrite dies, who gets the Deathrite ability?

a.canon: The King's controller, since Deathrite triggers while the units are technically still in the realm.

q.canon: What happens if a second King of the Realm enters play?

a.canon: See 'Example - Two Kings of the Realm' in the codex.

links.name: Example - Two Kings of the Realm

q.canon: If my opponent plays a Mortal with a Genesis ability and I have a King in play, who gets the Genesis ability?

a.canon: The player with the King gets the benefit, since they control the Mortal as soon as it's in play.

q.canon: If Kingdom of Agartha's ability is active, can I choose to summon minions underground without a printed Burrowing ability?

a.canon: Yes. Kingdom of Agartha affects minions everywhere.

q.canon: When is Kingdom of Agartha's ability active?

a.canon: Whenever you have three earth affinity! It is not optional; it's a passive ability that's always on while you have the necessary affinity.

q.canon: How does this interact with Court Jester?

a.canon: You don't get to look at your opponent's hand, but you do get to choose which of their cards they discard (e.g. site or spell).

q.canon: If two are played, which one takes precedence?

a.canon: The most recently played one. See 'ongoing effects' for more details.

q.canon: If there are two in play (and mine was played first), then I drop mine and pick it back up, do I take precedence?

a.canon: No. Competing passive abilities are tracked based on when the card entered play.

q.canon: What happens if the power of one of the units changes during the resolution of this effect so that it's no longer weaker?

a.canon: Only check that the target is weaker when it is initially targeted, and when the effect first starts to resolve from the storyline. Once the effect is resolving and minions are moving, it does not matter if the relative powers change after that point.

q.canon: What happens if I cast Lacuna Entity to a void location and then pull in a minion with a passive ability which will silence or disable the Entity?

a.canon: If the Entity pulls in something which will remove its abilities (e.g. Sisters of Silence) then the Entity will briefly find itself in the void without the voidwalk ability, and will be banished. It will have already pulled the other minion to its location, however. Note that if it pulls in a minion which disables other minions 'at rest,' such as a Hillock Basilisk, the Entity will not be at rest until after that minion has finished moving and passives are applied. This means the Basilisk would be banished before it could disable the Entity.

q.canon: What happens if I have a minion that occupies more than one site (e.g. Mountain Giant) and also carries Land Deed?

a.canon: Land Deed only grants you control of the site that Land Deed occupies.

q.canon: If I gain control of a site in the middle of my turn, does it produce mana immediately?

a.canon: No. Sites produce mana at the start of your turn and when they enter the realm. Since the site with Land Deed was already in the realm, it doesn't produce mana merely because you took control of it.

q.canon: What happens if I have a Land Deed on Rubble?

a.canon: You control the Rubble and your avatar will lose life if the Rubble takes damage, but the Rubble still doesn't provide mana. i.e. you own a hunk of worthless rock!

q.canon: What counts as a 'fire spell'?

a.canon: Once a minion, aura, or artifact enters the realm, it is no longer considered a 'spell.' Magic never enters the realm, so it is still considered a spell while it is resolving. In effect, Lava Salamander is immune to fire Magic.

q.canon: Does this card count as an 'attack' since it has the word 'attack' in its name?

a.canon: Sorry for the confusion, but no, this is not actually an attack! You only get an 'attack' from the Move and Attack basic ability, or card text that specifically uses the word attack (e.g. Crave Golem). This card text uses the word 'strike,' which means the unit simply deals damage equal to its power (and there's no chance for the opponent to Defend, and you can strike Stealthed or Airborne units, etc.)

q.canon: What if there are fewer than three cards in the chosen collection?

a.canon: You banish all of the remaining cards.

q.canon: Can I lightning bolt the void?

a.canon: Yes, but only if the spellcaster is in the void (since Lightning Bolt targets, the spellcaster must be in the same region).

q.canon: What happens if Lilith summons a minion with an end of turn ability (e.g. Infernal Legion)?

a.canon: Their ability will not trigger this turn.

q.canon: Who controls the summoned minion?

a.canon: The controller of Lilith. Note cards always go to the cemetery of their owner, regardless of their controller.

q.canon: Do I summon a copy the turn I first summon the Locusts?

a.canon: Yes! At the end of the turn you first summon them, they will see that there are no 'new' Locusts (meaning Locusts summoned by the triggered ability), and thus summon a copy. The following turn if you still have two in the realm, you'll only get one more.

q.canon: What does 'defend alone' mean?

a.canon: When the Defend window closes (see 'Attack' in the codex for details), If only a single enemy unit uses the Defend ability, the Defender is removed from the fight and the original attack target is reinstated. Defenders still arrive one at a time, but if there's only one, the defense effectively is negated (though that one defender still got to tap and move to the attack's location).

q.canon: How do I properly resolve this effect?
