a.canon: Lord of Greed may and must take a carriable artifact from anywhere in the realm, including from another unit sharing a location with him. In this case, 'elsewhere' means anywhere other than Lord of Greed's hands! He will take from allies as well. This does not target the artifact, so even artifacts carried by minions with stealth are not safe from Lord of Greed.

q.canon: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?

a.canon: The beta text is correct.

q.canon: Can my allied minion tempt an enemy in a different region to take a step closer?

a.canon: Yes, as long as they occupy a nearby site, they can be above or below that site. However, they cannot be tempted to take a step into a region they couldn't normally move into (e.g. they cannot be made to step underground if they do not have Burrowing).

q.canon: If the tempted enemy has multiple equally closer steps, who chooses the specific step taken?

a.canon: The caster of this spell determines among the equally closer choices.

q.canon: If Maddening Bells tries to increase the cost of a spell that has an alternate casting cost of zero (e.g. Deathspeaker ability while on death's door, Aramos Mercenaries), what happens?

a.canon: The spell costs zero. See 'Cost' for more details.

q.canon: When summoning minions, does Maddening Bells care about the location where the minion is summoned, or where the spellcaster is?

a.canon: Only where the spellcaster is, not the summoning location.

q.canon: If the Spellcaster is nearby Maddening Bells but the spell affects something not nearby, does it still cost 2 extra mana?

a.canon: Yes. Maddening Bells's ability only cares about the Spellcaster's position.

q.canon: Does the movement get resolved simultaneously?

a.canon: Yes, all the steps are simultaneously resolved (which might then provoke a variety of triggers).

q.canon: If I choose to pull a minion, do I have to pull all minions?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Can I use Floodplain before Maelström triggers?

a.canon: No. Floodplain is an activated ability, which can only be activated during your Main Phase.

q.canon: Consider the group of sites below. An oversized minion occupies 1-2-4-5. Maelström is #5. Can the oversized minion be pulled in any way?

a.canon: Yes. When pulling or pushing an oversized unit, choose a single location the oversized unit occupies (and meets the requirement of the effect), and push/pull from there. So, assuming Sites 2 and 4 are water sites as well, you could choose Site 2: Oversized minion is pulled South, and ends up at 4-5-7-8. OR, choose Site 4: Oversized minion is pulled East, and ends up at 2-3-5-6. OR, choose Site 5: Oversized minion isn't pulled at all.

q.canon: If Magellan Globe is in play, can an aura or an oversized unit be cast on the edge of the realm, spanning the realm?

a.canon: Yes. Ensure that the game state is clear, so all players know which sites the aura occupies, using notes as needed.

q.canon: What happens if I cast a spell that does grid-based damage?

a.canon: The grid can span edges of the realm as needed, since they are connected.

q.canon: Will effects that check 'adjacent' or 'nearby' (e.g. Poison Nova) span edges of the realm?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Can projectiles go around the edges of the realm?

a.canon: Yes, as long as they don't change regions. There are exactly four regions in Sorcery: Surface, Void, Underwater, Underground.

q.canon: Can I play Earthquake or other similar 2x2 area effects around the edge of the realm with Magellan Globe in play?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Can Airborne units in one corner of the realm fly directly to the opposite corner if Magellan Globe is in the realm?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If Magellan Globe is in play and an Oversized unit on the top row moves 'up' one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?

a.canon: Since Magellan Globe is an ongoing effect that connects the top and bottom edges, the oversized unit can occupy 2 locations on the top row and 2 locations on the bottom row. Ensure that game state is clear, using notes as needed.

q.canon: If Magellan Globe leaves play when a card is spanning the edge of the realm, what happens?

a.canon: Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for a minion, it dies. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for an avatar, shrink it until there is a legal position (Avatar controller's choice), and place it there.

q.canon: Are there any other corner cases for Magellan Globe?

a.canon: I think you mean edge cases! Let us know if you think of any more we should add. In general, apply the golden rule and have fun!

q.canon: What if an effect directs me to draw a spell, but it turns out there's a site on top of my spellbook?

a.canon: All cards in your spellbook are considered spells while in your spellbook, so you can draw it normally.

q.canon: What if an effect directs me to draw a site?

a.canon: You have no atlas, and thus any effect that causes you to draw sites will not resolve. You don't draw any cards and you don't lose the game. You cannot choose to draw from your atlas in your start phase.

q.canon: What if an effect specifies a spell or site from a zone other than my spellbook?

a.canon: If an effect cares about spell vs. site while the card is outside of your spellbook, you must follow the effect correctly at the moment the effect resolves. Several examples: If resolve Stone Rain, you must honestly state how many sites you have in your hand at that moment. You can partially remove cards from their sleeves and show the back to demonstrate the accurate count to your opponent, or call a judge in a tournament if you have foil cards (or double sleeve your cards with different inner color sleeves in the case of foils). If your opponent plays Pith Imp, you must honestly specify your spells in hand, and randomly select from only those. If your opponent attacks your Wizard's Den for the first time and you don't have any spells in hand, you must honestly demonstrate to your opponent that you only have sites in hand. If you play Sisters of Avalon and have no spells in hand, you must honestly demonstrate to your opponent that you have no spells. After an effect resolves that requires you to reveal the number of spells and sites in your hand, you may then mix up the cards in your hand again so that your opponent doesn't know which cards are spells and which are sites.

q.canon: Am I required to sleeve my cards, and if so, how should I do it?

a.canon: You are required to sleeve your cards, and they should all be the same. Cards in your spellbook and collection should be indistinguishable whether they are sites or spells.

q.canon: If I do 1 damage to three minions simultaneously, does the Barricade break?

a.canon: Yes, because 1+1+1 = 3 damage dealt all at the same time.

q.canon: What if this is animated by an Enchantress?

a.canon: If an animated Mariner's Curse moves and enters a water site, it will submerge itself (if possible) and die (assuming it doesn't have Submerge). If it hasn't died, it will then return itself to its owner's hand. It will not have a chance to attack before its effect resolves, because the move happens before the attack.

q.canon: If I Grapple Shot a minion with Submerge through an area affected by Mariner's Curse, what happens?

a.canon: When the Grapple Shot projectile hits the unit, the game adds specific movement steps for the ally to the Storyline: Move A (surface) -> B (surface), Move B (surface) -> C (surface). Then, we start resolving those steps. If Mariner's Curse is on site B, once the unit being dragged reaches site B, it will be submerged, and live. Then the game tries to resolve Move B (surface) -> C (surface), which fails, since the unit isn't on the surface of site B anymore. Thus, there's no strike from Grapple Shot since it didn't reach the hit unit's location.

q.canon: An oversized unit occupies a specific site and then moves. After the move, it still occupies that site. Did it enter the site?

a.canon: No. It was already there, and remained there (though it may have entered different sites due to its move).

q.canon: If I double twice, is it multiplied by 4?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: What happens if the striking unit and the unit-being-struck are at different locations (e.g. from a unit with the Ranged ability, or Quarrelsome Kobolds)?

a.canon: The strike occurs at the location of the unit being struck. If the unit being struck is nearby the Mask, they will take double damage.

q.canon: My minion starts nearby the Mask and thus must attack. During my Move and Attack mandatory action, my minion moves so that it's no longer near the Mask. Do I still have to attack?

a.canon: No, since you do not actually attack until after moving. If your minion is no longer nearby the Mask, you are not required to attack after moving.

q.canon: What does it mean to 'permanently lose stealth'?

a.canon: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

q.canon: Once the Master Tracker leaves play, does a future enemy that arrives with Stealth still have stealth?

a.canon: Yes. But enemies that already lost Stealth won't regain it.

q.canon: Does this buff my opponent's Mortals as well?

a.canon: Yes! The Mayor wants as many votes as possible!

q.canon: Can this Genesis effect drag a minion into a different region?

a.canon: Yes, due to the golden rule. Because avatars cannot enter non-surface locations, if one is being dragged by this effect they will be dragged as far as they can while staying within the surface region.

q.canon: If I play Dodge Roll on my Megamoeba, does the attack still go through because the Megamoeba is still occupying the original location?

a.canon: Yes, the target is still valid, but Megamoeba now has +1 power from the extra location it occupies thanks to Dodge Roll.

q.canon: If my opponent uses an effect that moves sites (e.g. Atlas Wanderer, Earthquake, etc.), what happens?

a.canon: Megamoeba moves with the site. Megamoeba is mostly treated a normal size unit for movement effects.

q.canon: If Megamoeba starts at 2 power, can it move into Gnome Hollows (thus getting to 3 power)?

a.canon: Yes. First, Megamoeba enters, then it grows in power immediately after entering.

q.canon: What happens if Megamoeba is the target of Whirling Blades?

a.canon: The Megamoeba moves 2 steps by extending a pseudopod twice (possibly from two different starting locations), and gains 2 power. Then, it strikes all enemies in the starting and destination locations of the pseudopods that took the steps.

q.canon: When the Megamoeba is teleported, does its passive ability still apply?

a.canon: Yes. A single pseudopod enters the teleportation destination, and the Megamoeba can become a single oversized unit that spans non-adjacent squares. The Megamoeba is weird.

q.canon: What happens if Megamoeba is in a Silence aura?

a.canon: As soon as it enters the Silence aura, it loses its abilities, but size is considered a characteristic and thus persists. Therefore, it continues to occupy all the locations, but it doesn't get the +1 power per location. It will move like any other oversized unit (albeit potentially strangely shaped).

q.canon: Can Megamoeba declare a movement to a location it already occupies? (e.g. if it wanted to move an artifact it was carrying)

a.canon: Yes. Megamoeba is weird.

q.canon: What happens when Megamoeba gets pulled / pushed?

a.canon: Choose a specific location it occupies and pull / push a single pseudopod from there.

q.canon: If the Megamoeba occupies a site with an enemy, can the Megamoeba take the Move and Attack basic ability to move first, and then attack that original enemy, thus growing in power beforehand?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If the Megamoeba occupies a site with an enemy, and the Megamoeba moves to a different site without attacking, can the enemy intercept?

a.canon: Yes! If Megamoeba uses Move and Attack, then doesn't attack, any enemy that shares a location with them may tap to intercept.

q.canon: What happens if Megamoeba gains burrow or submerge?

a.canon: It can occupy both the surface location and the subsurface location on a site, and each occupied location will grant +1 power, per card text. 40 power Megamoeba, here we come!

q.canon: What happens if Megamoeba is forcefully burrowed or submerged without the burrow or submerge ability?

a.canon: If any part of unit occupies an inhospitable location, it dies. So, the Megamoeba would die in this case.

q.canon: What happens when the Megamoeba gets carried?

a.canon: It occupied all the locations it was carried through.

q.canon: How do I resolve this effect?

a.canon: If you cast Mephistopheles, your Avatar is banished. Mephistopheles is now your Avatar. He retains Unique rarity, Demon type, and Air element, but he's no longer a minion and only an Avatar. Your current and maximum life remain the same. Notably, you won't be able to play sites normally because Mephistopheles doesn't have that ability. You will still be able to cast spells because Avatars are spellcasters as one of their characteristics. If you manage to summon Mephistopheles without casting him, then he will not replace your avatar, but his second ability will still function.

q.canon: How does Merlin's ability work and what does 'any time' actually permit?

a.canon: This is a passive ability, usable any time on your turn, including during your start phase before you draw a card. But, you may still only cast spells when they are normally permitted to be cast (i.e. during your Main Phase when nothing else is on the storyline other than this ability). Technically, if a Crave Golem were attacking during your Start Phase, Merlin could cast a Dodge Roll then!

q.canon: Can I choose sites that share a corner?

a.canon: Yes. 'Border' means adjacent squares, not including diagonals.

q.canon: What happens if this is cast from a cemetery by Deathspeaker?

a.canon: You can still use its optional alternate summoning ability to transform an artifact into the Mimic, and then the Mimic will be banished.

q.canon: How does this ability work?

a.canon: When you summon Mimic, you can choose to summon it normally, or instead you can choose a carriable artifact anywhere in the realm. That artifact is banished, and the Mimic is placed at the artifact's location instead as it transforms. You control the Mimic, and if the artifact did not enter the realm this turn, the Mimic doesn't have Summoning Sickness. It turns out that artifact was a Mimic in disguise all along!

q.canon: If multiple minions including Miracle Workers die at the same time on Geistwood, can Miracle Workers return themselves and/or another minion that's dying to your hand?

a.canon: No, because Miracle Workers only return minions from the cemetery, and deathrites resolve while the minions are still in the realm. The Miracle Workers could return other minions that died earlier that turn and were in the cemetery.

q.canon: What happens if I try to use Mirage's alternate play text when it's played via Pathfinder?

a.canon: Assuming you own and control the adjacent site, Mirage's ability can modify the play restrictions on Pathfinder, allowing you to return the site to your hand.

q.canon: How do Smokestacks of Gnaak and Mirror Realm interact?

a.canon: By the time Mirror Realm enters the realm, it's already a copy. Thus, it can copy a nearby site, and then promptly loses all abilities of that copied site (but still is the copy, without abilities). See 'Apply Ongoing Effects In Order' in the codex for nitty-gritty details.

q.canon: What if Mirror Realm loses its abilities after it enters play (e.g. Smokestacks of Gnaak is played later)?

a.canon: Mirror Realm remains a copy, but any abilities that were printed on the original site are now ignored.

q.canon: Does Mirror Realm also copy the rarity of the chosen site?

a.canon: Yes, it's as if you had the exact same card.

q.canon: Can Mirror Realm copy Rift Valley and enter the realm in the special way, as long as it ends up nearby the Rift Valley that it's copying?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: What happens if Mirror Realm copies a Rubble?

a.canon: If Mirror Realm copies a Rubble, you gain no mana. You still control the Rubble, it can be attacked normally, you can play sites adjacent to it, it can be replaced by a site normally, etc. Track it carefully, distinct from other uncontrolled Rubble in the realm.

q.canon: Once this is in play, do I put cards into the cemetery that I own or the cemetery that I control?

a.canon: You always put your cards into the cemetery you own (the one nearby your deck).

q.canon: If I have Wormelow Tump in play, what happens?

a.canon: The cemeteries are still swapped, and you protect everything in 'your' cemetery (which is really your opponent's).

q.canon: If there are an even number of Mismanaged Mortuaries in play, do they cancel out?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: For Mock Court, Court of Equity, and Mobbed Court, do these effects stack with themselves if multiple copies are in the realm?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: For Mock Court, Court of Equity, and Mobbed Court, do these effects stack with themselves if multiple copies are in the realm?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: For Mock Court, how does this extra cost work?

a.canon: For each ordinary minion that you would summon, you must pay 1 mana at the moment it would be summoned into the realm (for each copy of Mock Court). This is not an additional casting cost; it's a summoning cost. If you can pay it, you must. If you are summoning multiple ordinary minions simultaneously (e.g. Border Militia) and can't afford to pay for all of them, you may choose which ones you pay for. Any that you cannot pay for are not summoned. This effect applies to ordinary token minions (e.g. Skeletons, Frogs, Foot Soldiers) that are summoned without being cast, as well as ordinary minions that you cast normally (e.g. Apprentice Wizard).

q.canon: If I transform an enemy minion into a Monster from my hand or Horrible Hybrids from my collection, who controls it?

a.canon: The controller of the minion does not change when transforming, so in that case your opponent would control it. Note cards always go to their owner's cemetery so when that minion dies it will go to your cemetery.

q.canon: Since this 'counts as Grey Wolves' does that mean I can include any number of it in my spellbook?

a.canon: No. The phrase 'counts as Grey Wolves' means that other cards will see it as being named 'Grey Wolves' in addition to its normal name. You still must follow rarity restrictions.

q.canon: Where do I keep Morgana's hand of cards?

a.canon: See 'Only It Can Cast' in the codex.

q.canon: What happens to Morgana's hand if she is silenced or disabled?

a.canon: Her hand of cards continues to exist in its own zone, though Morgana can no longer cast those spells without the Spellcaster ability. Since you control Morgana, you can still look at the cards.

q.canon: What happens my opponent gains control of my Morgana?

a.canon: Your opponent will be able to have Morgana cast the spells in her hand, assuming they have the mana and appropriate threshold. You can't look at the cards in her hand while you don't control her. Remember that cards always return to their owner's cemetery, hand, or decks when leaving the realm after being played from Morgana's hand, regardless of who controls her.

q.canon: What happens to Morgana's hand if she is transformed into something else? A frog, for instance?!

a.canon: If Morgana is transformed, the ongoing effect which created her hand of cards will continue to apply, and the hand will continue to exist. If Morgana's new form does not have the ability to cast spells, she will not be able to cast them, but if she becomes a spellcaster again she will still have access to her hand.

q.canon: Does 'here' mean Mother Nature's location or site?

a.canon: 'Here' references Mother Nature's exact location.

q.canon: When I flee, is it step by step movement or teleportation?

a.canon: It's step by step movement!

q.canon: After fleeing, if I somehow fail to reach the Sanctuary, do I still gain the Ward?

a.canon: No!

q.canon: What path can I choose when resolving this ability?

a.canon: See Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic in the Codex.

links.name: Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic

q.canon: What happens if a Mountain Giant occupies a Silence aura?

a.canon: A card's size is generally set when it enters the realm, and is considered one of its characteristics, not an ability. It will not resize.

q.canon: If Polar Explorers or Ruler of Thul are in play and an oversized unit on the top row moves 'up' one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?

a.canon: This ability only allows movement across the borders, not ongoing occupation. Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied.

q.canon: If Magellan Globe is in play and an Oversized unit on the top row moves 'up' one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?

a.canon: Since Magellan Globe is an ongoing effect that connects the top and bottom edges, the oversized unit can occupy 2 locations on the top row and 2 locations on the bottom row. Ensure that game state is clear, using notes as needed.

q.canon: If Magellan Globe leaves play when a card is spanning the edge of the realm, what happens?

a.canon: Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for a minion, it dies. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for an avatar, shrink it until there is a legal position (Avatar controller's choice), and place it there.

q.canon: You have a minion on my Mountain Pass. Can I summon a minion on the site?

a.canon: Yes. Though summoning is included in 'entering,' it is not moving on the ground. So you can summon all you want, since summoning isn't moving.

q.canon: Your minion attacks my Mountain Pass. Can my adjacent minion defend?

a.canon: No, assuming the minion is beginning on the surface of a site and doesn't have the airborne ability. Because another minion is already on the surface of the Mountain Pass, that location will not be within your minion's range of motion, and so it cannot activate the defend ability.

q.canon: What does 'enter this site on the ground' mean?

a.canon: Entering on the ground only covers movement from the surface of another site to the surface of the Mountain Pass, excluding Airborne and teleportation.

q.canon: I have a minion on my Mountain Pass, and a voidwalk minion on an adjacent square. Can I move from the void to Mountain Pass?

a.canon: Yes, since moving on the ground requires the unit to start from the surface of a site. Since the void isn't a site, moving from the void to Mountain Pass isn't considered moving on the ground.

q.canon: Once I target the site, do I also pick 'surface' or 'unburrow?'

a.canon: No, you simply target the site, and then the proper action is applied. If a water site is the target, minions there are surfaced. If a land site is the target, minions there are unburrowed.

q.canon: Do I pick left or right for all units together, or can I choose different directions?

a.canon: Choose left or right, and apply it to every unit at land sites in the column.

q.canon: Does this effect span the void?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: The alpha, alternate art version of this card from the pledge pack has the text 'Spellcaster nearby,' while the regular foil and non-foil versions have the text 'Spellcaster here.' which is correct?

a.canon: The normal version is correct. The text should be 'Spellcaster here.' The alternate art version is not legal for tournament play.

q.canon: Does this ability protect my minions from movement effects like forceful burrowing (e.g. Bury), submerge (e.g. Drown), and teleportation (e.g. Chaos Twister)?

a.canon: Yes, all of those effects are movement. With Chaos Twister, don't even attempt to blow the card if the target is an ally nearby Old Salt Anchorman.

q.canon: Does this ability prevent my opponent from rearranging sites? (e.g. Earthquake, Atlas Wanderers)

a.canon: No, your opponent can still rearrange sites, because that doesn't count as moving the units, just the sites.

q.canon: Does this ability stop effects which cause an ally to take their own steps (e.g. Guile Sirens, Coy Nixie, Lure)?

a.canon: No. Sailors historically have trouble resisting the siren's call.

q.canon: How does this Magic work?

a.canon: Onslaught creates an ongoing effect which lasts the duration of your turn and continually prevents your units from being immobilized, silenced, or disabled. A minion cast after Onslaught resolves would be protected, and would gain +1 power and Charge. Note that Onslaught does not remove any ongoing effects which may be disabling, silencing or immobilizing your units, it just suppresses them for the duration of your turn. For example, if you play Onslaught and then summon a Slumbering Giantess, her Genesis ability will still resolve, and she will be disabled when the effect of Onslaught wears off. For the duration of your turn, however, she will have +1 power and Charge, and will ignore the disable effect from her Genesis ability.

q.canon: When does this artifact provide mana?

a.canon: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller's turn.

q.canon: Is the Orb the spellcaster for the copied spell?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If I cast a Magic with X in the cost, does the copy have the same value of X too?

a.canon: Yes. The Orb copies the spell after costs have been paid, so X is a set value.

q.canon: If I cast a spell with an additional cost (e.g. Craterize), do I need to pay the additional cost again?

a.canon: No. The Orb copies the spell after costs have been paid.

q.canon: Can I target the same site twice when casting two copies of Craterize with Orb?

a.canon: You technically can, but beware! If the first Craterize successfully destroys the targeted site, the second Craterize will no longer have a valid target in the realm and will fail, resulting in no damage from that copy of Craterize.

q.canon: Who controls the copied Magic?

a.canon: The original caster of that Magic controls the copy made by the Orb.

q.canon: If Order of the White Wing is summoned along with other minions simultaneously (e.g. Boneyard, Golden Dawn, etc.), what happens?

a.canon: All the simultaneously summoned minions enter the realm successfully. The Order of the White Wing's ability only applies once it's in the realm.

q.canon: Does the minion that's being summoned from elsewhere enter the realm for a moment before it's banished?

a.canon: No, it doesn't ever enter the realm. For example, it will not trigger a Genesis, it will not get a Lance, it will not trigger a Mariner's Curse, etc. It doesn't actually enter the realm at all, since this is a replacement effect.

q.canon: Does this prevent minions from being cast from other 'hand' zones (e.g. Morgana le Fay, or an Omphalos)?

a.canon: Yes. The Order prevents minions from being summoned from anywhere except directly from a player's hand.

q.canon: Does the target need to be in the same region as the Harpooneers?

a.canon: No. Normally the answer is yes, but the card text 'above or below' means that normal targeting restrictions are ignored, and the Harpooneers can be in any region (surface, underground, underwater, or in the void). As long as there is an adjacent Water site to the Harpooneers and a minion occupying that water site, it will get pulled to the Harpooneers' location.

q.canon: Does the 'adjacent Water site' need to be in the same region as the Harpooneers?

a.canon: No. Because the Water site is not targeted, and because the card text uses 'site' instead of 'location,' the site does not need to be in the same region as the Harpooneers.

q.canon: On my turn when I go to Death's Door, can I still take damage and lose life?

a.canon: Yes. You cannot lose the game due to taking damage, but taking damage and losing life will reduce your life total if possible. See 'Death's Door' for more details.

q.canon: Does Overflowing Court disable other Overflowing Courts? Other cards with 'Court' in the title?

a.canon: Yes. Any card with the exact word 'Court' in the title will be disabled. For example, Mock Court and Court Jester would be disabled, but Courtesan Thaïs is not.

q.canon: If a non-minion (e.g. River of Flame, or Orb of Ba'al Berith) is the spellcaster, can I sacrifice it?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: Do you round up your life loss, or round up your ending life?

a.canon: Round up the life loss. For example, if you had 3 life, you'd lose 2, ending up at 1.

q.canon: Does this cause a zero power unit to deal 2 damage when striking?

a.canon: Yes, this effect will cause zero power units to strike for 2 damage.

q.canon: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?

a.canon: The beta text is correct.

q.canon: Where does Pathfinder play its first site turn 1?

a.canon: You must play your first site turn 1 under the Pathfinder per the game rules.

q.canon: Does Pristine Paradise provide mana the turn the Pathfinder plays it from the atlas? That is, does the site have enough time to make mana before the Pathfinder moves onto it?

a.canon: Yes, sites immediately generate mana when they come into play.

q.canon: What happens if I try to use Mirage's alternate play text when it's played via Pathfinder?

a.canon: Assuming you own and control the adjacent site, Mirage's ability can modify the play restrictions on Pathfinder, allowing you to return the site to your hand.

q.canon: If I have no sites but it's not the first turn (e.g. Roots of Yggdrasil destroyed everything) and I use the Pathfinder's ability, am I forced to play the site under the Pathfinder's current location, or could I play the site adjacent?

a.canon: Since it's not the first turn of the game, you aren't forced to play under yourself. The Pathfinder offers an alternate way to play sites, and thus you could play it adjacent if you wanted.

q.canon: What happens if I try to use Rift Valley's ability when it's played via Pathfinder?

a.canon: When using the Pathfinder's ability, you reveal the site, then play it in an adjacent Rubble or void (then Pathfinder moves there). With Rift Valley, you could use its ability to make a void adjacent to Pathfinder, then play it there (and Pathfinder would then move there).

q.canon: Can I use this ability even if I'm surrounded by sites, in the hopes that Rift Valley is on top of my atlas?

a.canon: Yes, you may use the ability. Assuming a normal site (and not Rift Valley) is on top of your atlas, you'll reveal it, do nothing, and then put it back on top of your atlas.

q.canon: If Pathfinder cannot move to the played site because of some effect (e.g. Sphere of Animosity, Quagmire) can you still play the site?

a.canon: Yes, you can still play the site to a void or rubble adjacent to the Pathfinder, even if you know you cannot move to it (Sphere of Animosity) or an effect from the played site immediately stops the Pathfinder from being able to move (Quagmire).

q.canon: Can I use Ersatz Platz's ability to play a site from my collection?

a.canon: No, Pathfinder's ability specifies that the site must come from the top of your Atlas.

q.canon: Do both units need to have been in play for a turn or have charge?

a.canon: Yes. Summoning sick units can't be tapped to pay costs.

q.canon: What does 'can't attack you' actually mean?

a.canon: The other player can't attack anything you control (units or sites).

q.canon: If some effect prevents me from giving the Peace Offering to the other player (i.e. King Arthur), can they attack me on their next turn?

a.canon: Yes. If the other player does not end up controlling the Peace Offering after the ability resolves and passives are applied, you have not successfully given it to them, and they will be free to attack you.

q.canon: If Peace Offering leaves the realm, does the truce still apply?

a.canon: Yes, once the Peace Offering has been given to your opponent, they can't attack you next turn, regardless of what happens to the Peace Offering after that.

q.canon: Can a unit be moved through the top border of this site by force?

a.canon: No, assuming the unit does not have the Airborne ability. Effects which drag/push/pull a unit cannot cause it to move through the top border of this site while on the ground. For instance, a non-Airborne minion cannot use Grapple Shot to pass through this border, and a Pudge Butcher cannot pull a non-Airborne unit through it. Teleport effects do not pass through borders, however, and are not considered movement on the ground, so they can allow a unit to move to a location on the other side.

q.canon: Can I brand an enemy and step toward the closest Evil on the same turn?

a.canon: No, you must choose only one option each turn.

q.canon: Can I brand an enemy in a different region, or one with Stealth?

a.canon: Yes! Branding does not target, and therefore you can choose minions in different regions and/or those with Stealth. This can combo successfully with other cards that care about minions being Evil!

q.canon: Can I brand an enemy who can't be modified, e.g. Monks of Kobalsa?

a.canon: Yes, you can still brand them, and your cards will still treat them as Evil. They aren't actually being modified or becoming Evil; your cards just treat them that way.

q.canon: If my opponent has a warded minion and I brand it as Evil, does it lose Ward?

a.canon: No, because only your cards treat it as Evil. Also, branding does not target, so Ward won't break for that reason either.

q.canon: When determining 'closest Evil,' do I only consider units in my region?

a.canon: Yes! See 'Closest' for more details.

q.canon: What happens when a minion carries another minion that's carrying a minion?

a.canon: Only the minions you're directly carrying count against your limit. Have fun at the carnival!

q.canon: How does the Philosopher's Stone work with multi-element cards, such as King Arthur and Queen Guienevere? Would King Arthur, who requires 4 mana, cost 3 or 0 Mana to cast using the Stone?

a.canon:
Cards that have different element symbols count as a spell of each of those affinities. So Arthur and Guinevere are each an Air spell, an Earth spell, a Fire spell, and a Water spell, all at the same time. But you are still casting them together as a single spell. So, assuming Arthur is your spellcaster's first spell of the turn, the Stone will offer a discount of 1 mana for Arthur, making him cost 3 mana.
This also means that when Arthur is played he uses up the Stone for that spellcaster's turn because he's simultaneously the first Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spell played this turn. So the Spellcaster cannot continue to use the stone that turn.

q.canon: If I have two (e.g. via Replication), do the effects stack?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: What happens if a second Pied Piper of Hameln enters play?

a.canon: You apply each of their abilities in timestamp order. The first Piper takes control of all minions with 1 or less power, then the second Piper will take control of them. The controller of the second Piper will end up controlling all minions with 1 or less power.

q.canon: What happens if the minion which leaves this site can't be warded (e.g. it has a Ward already or it's Evil)?

a.canon: The Ward remains on the site, as it cannot be transferred.

q.canon: How does this interact with effects which modify healing (e.g. River of Blood)?

a.canon: You banish all dead minions, count them, and then heal once for a total amount equal to the number of dead minions which were banished. River of Blood would halve, rounding down, that final total.

q.canon: Where does the stolen spell go?

a.canon: It goes to a separate zone as if the Pith Imp was carrying the spell; it does not go to your hand. You may look at the spell and your opponent may not (though they do get to see the spell at the moment you steal it).

q.canon: If Pith Imp somehow gains Spellcaster, can it pretty please cast the spell it stole?

a.canon: Yes, that does seem fun!

q.canon: Where can I summon the frogs?

a.canon: You choose one location anywhere in the realm, and then all 7 frogs are summoned to that location.

q.canon: If Polar Explorers or Ruler of Thul are in play and an oversized unit on the top row moves 'up' one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?

a.canon: This ability only allows movement across the borders, not ongoing occupation. Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied.

q.canon: Does a pollimorphed animated aura (e.g. Enchantress) return to an aura form later?

a.canon: No. It is permanently a Frog token, and occupies a single location.

q.canon: If the original minion occupied more than one location, what happens?

a.canon: The controller of the transformation effect chooses which location the Frog token occupies.

q.canon: Does Pristine Paradise provide mana the turn the Pathfinder plays it from the atlas? That is, does the site have enough time to make mana before the Pathfinder moves onto it?

a.canon: Yes, sites immediately generate mana when they come into play.

q.canon: If the genesis resolves, and then my opponent plays Smokestacks of Gnaak nearby, does the Quagmire effect continue?

a.canon: Yes. The genesis ability creates an effect that lasts until the start of your next turn.

q.canon: How does the Philosopher's Stone work with multi-element cards, such as King Arthur and Queen Guienevere? Would King Arthur, who requires 4 mana, cost 3 or 0 Mana to cast using the Stone?

a.canon:
Cards that have different element symbols count as a spell of each of those affinities. So Arthur and Guinevere are each an Air spell, an Earth spell, a Fire spell, and a Water spell, all at the same time. But you are still casting them together as a single spell. So, assuming Arthur is your spellcaster's first spell of the turn, the Stone will offer a discount of 1 mana for Arthur, making him cost 3 mana.
This also means that when Arthur is played he uses up the Stone for that spellcaster's turn because he's simultaneously the first Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spell played this turn. So the Spellcaster cannot continue to use the stone that turn.

q.canon: Does this end of turn ability cause the Beast to lose stealth?

a.canon: No, as it is a triggered ability it does not cause the Beast to interact with the realm.

q.canon: Where can I summon the raised minion?

a.canon: After randomly determining the dead minion, you may summon it anywhere.

q.canon: Does this destroy artifacts underneath the site, or just ones on the surface?

a.canon: Artifacts both above and below the site are destroyed.

q.canon: How does this ability work?

a.canon: Whenever Realm-Eater attacks a site and strikes it, that site is destroyed and the Realm-Eater gains an ongoing effect causing it to be immobile. You can activate Realm-Eater's digest ability to remove one instance of this immobilizing effect, but if you have attacked and destroyed multiple sites you must digest each one.

q.canon: What happens if Realm-Eater cannot be immobilized due to some effect (e.g. Tabula Rasa, Onslaught)?

a.canon: For as long as the effect is being applied, Realm-Eater can ignore the ongoing effect caused by eating sites. If that effect is removed, Realm-Eater will no longer be immune to the lethargy caused by eating so much, and will be immobilized if they have not cleared the ongoing effects by digesting the sites.

q.canon: What does 'Artifacts can't be carried here' mean?

a.canon: Artifacts which share a location with the Red Rock are no longer carried. They are not dropped, they just stop being carried, so the effect will still apply to artifacts which cannot be dropped. These artifacts also cannot be targeted by the Pick Up ability.

q.canon: How is this resolved if either the artifact or the bearer cannot be pulled?

a.canon: If the bearer of the artifact cannot be pulled, but the artifact can, the Red Rock pulls the artifact out of the bearer's hands. If the artifact cannot be pulled, neither the bearer nor the artifact are pulled.

q.canon: Does the Hyena stop being a Beast if it becomes a Demon?

a.canon: No, it will be both a Demon and a Beast.

q.canon: How does this ability work?

a.canon: If the Regurgitator has an empty belly and there are any dead minions, you must fill its belly by banishing one. If it has a full belly, you must empty it by shooting a projectile. If it has an empty belly and there are no dead minions, nothing happens.

q.canon: Can I play this with only one Hellhound in my collection?

a.canon: Yes. You will only summon that one Hellhound.

q.canon: Where can I conjure the copy?

a.canon: You can conjure it anywhere.

q.canon: How does this work?

a.canon: After the throw, Rhongomyniad is in the final location along its path, and is not carried by any unit.

q.canon: What happens when two things that strike first clash at the same time?

a.canon: If multiple units in the same fight have an ability that allows them to strike first, they strike at the same time. Then any surviving units without that ability make their strikes.

q.canon: Can I draw a site with this effect?

a.canon: Try this riddle: Which spell will I draw? Fooled you! Neither of them! (Yes, you can draw a site.)

q.canon: Can you 'pull apart' a row with a single site?

a.canon: No. That's not what 'pull apart' means.

q.canon: What is a technical definition of what's happening when you use this card's ability?

a.canon: Choose a row or column with two adjacent sites and at least one void. Then, 'pull apart' the two adjacent sites as follows: one site stays in its current square, and the other site (along with all other contiguous sites in its row or column) shifts one square. Put Rift Valley in the void that was just created. The shifting of sites and the arrival of Rift Valley happen simultaneously.

q.canon: Can you play Rift Valley into an area affected by Atlantean Fate?

a.canon: Yes, since Atlantean Fate only affects the site once it's already in play, and Rift Valley modifies how it's played in the first place.

q.canon: How do Smokestacks of Gnaak and Rift Valley interact?

a.canon: Rift Valley enters the realm using its ability, and only loses its ability once it's in the realm (which by then, it doesn't really matter).

q.canon: When pulling apart the row or column to place the site, can Rift Valley be played non-adjacent to your other sites?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Does this move oversized units or auras that occupy more than one square?

a.canon: No.

q.canon: What happens if I try to use Rift Valley's ability when it's played via Pathfinder?

a.canon: When using the Pathfinder's ability, you reveal the site, then play it in an adjacent Rubble or void (then Pathfinder moves there). With Rift Valley, you could use its ability to make a void adjacent to Pathfinder, then play it there (and Pathfinder would then move there).

q.canon: Can Mirror Realm copy Rift Valley and enter the realm in the special way, as long as it ends up nearby the Rift Valley that it's copying?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If I have no sites but it's not the first turn (e.g. Roots of Yggdrasil destroyed everything) and I play Rift Valley, am I forced to play the site under my avatar, or could I pull apart a row of Rubble and play it there?

a.canon: Since it's not the first turn of the game, you aren't forced to play under yourself. Rift Valley offers an alternate way to play a site, and thus you could pull apart a row and play it there if you wanted.

q.canon: If the damage from this trigger is prevented or redirected, do I still gain 1 life?

a.canon: No, you must deal at least 1 point of damage with the ability to gain any life.

q.canon: Can riptide pull a voidwalk minion in the void?

a.canon: No, because minions in the void aren't 'aboveground.'

q.canon: What are the details of pulling an oversized minion that occupies the water site and other locations?

a.canon: When pulling or pushing a oversized unit, choose a single location the oversized unit occupies (and meets the requirement of the effect - e.g. adjacent), and push/pull from there.

q.canon: If there are two Rivers of Blood in play, do they stack?

a.canon: Yes. Half the healing (rounding down), then half the healing again (round down). So Divine Healing would heal 1 with two Rivers of Blood in play.

q.canon: If River of Flame casts a spell, choosing the surface, but there are Maddening Bells underground, is the River of Flame affected?

a.canon: Yes! Those bells are so loud (and still nearby the caster).

q.canon: If River of Flame casts a spell, must you pick a region that it's casting from?

a.canon: Yes. Pick surface or underground when you cast the spell (or underwater if it's flooded).

q.canon: What is a 'connected river'?

a.canon: Connected rivers are a contiguous group of adjacent sites with River in their name, regardless of who controls them, and which contains River Rapids. River Rapids is, by definition, connected to itself, even if it is not connected to any other Rivers.

q.canon: How does this ability work?

a.canon: It is an activated ability that you can choose to activate one time on your turn. You choose a minion that is on a connected river, and push it one step. You can use this to push the minion off of rivers, and you can activate it even if River Rapids is the only 'connected' river.

q.canon: Can this ability push minions which are submerged at connected Rivers?

a.canon: Yes, submerged minions can be pushed.

q.canon: The term 'summon' means 'enter the realm.' So, does that mean I can play this minion for free?

a.canon: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon this minion.

q.canon: What happens if Magellan Globe is in play and I push it along a complete row or column?

a.canon: The Rolling Boulder continues until it would repeat a step (i.e. back to where it started), and then stops instead of repeating a step. It doesn't do 8 damage on the starting location, since a location is either along its path or not.

q.canon: If there are two units on a site and one of them uses the boulder, does the other one get damaged?

a.canon: Yes. It's dangerous to play with boulders.

q.canon: What path does the boulder take?

a.canon: It travels in a chosen cardinal direction, staying within the same region.

q.canon: What happens to destroyed Rubble?

a.canon: Nothing (it turns into more Rubble, and thus doesn't change).

q.canon: When exactly is 'after striking' ?

a.canon: After effects concurrent with striking (e.g. after gaining life via Daperyll Vampire), but before any Deathrite abilities resolve. It's in the same moment that Stealth would break due to striking.

q.canon: When does this artifact provide mana?

a.canon: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller's turn.

q.canon: If Polar Explorers or Ruler of Thul are in play and an oversized unit on the top row moves 'up' one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?

a.canon: This ability only allows movement across the borders, not ongoing occupation. Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied.

q.canon: Does 'no minion is Evil' mean they are no longer considered a Demon, Monster or Undead?

a.canon: Minions will still keep their Demon, Monster and Undead types! They simply are no longer Evil, and will not be affected by things which specifically affect Evil.

q.canon: If Persecutor brands a minion, are they still considered evil by that player's cards while the Saint of Redemption is in play?

a.canon: No, the Saint redeems all minions, and even the Persecutor's brand will not condemn a redeemed soul!

q.canon: Do all minions enter the realm tapped, or only minions which would have been Evil?

a.canon: All minion enter the realm tapped.

q.canon: Does this mean that minions which are not in the realm are not Evil as well?

a.canon: No minion anywhere is Evil as long as the Saint is in play. This means that if a player casts Black Mass, they will not be able to reveal any minions, as none of them can be Evil.

q.canon: Can I push an oversized unit?

a.canon: Yes, choose a cardinal direction and push the oversized unit one step in that direction as long as no part of the unit would change regions.

q.canon: Does the site itself get pushed?

a.canon: No.

q.canon: Can I choose different directions for each card being pushed?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Can I push something into another region?

a.canon: No, 'pushing' is a form of forced movement which cannot cause something to change regions unless it specifically says so.

q.canon: What does it mean to 'permanently lose stealth'?

a.canon: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

q.canon: A minion with Gilded Aegis is on a site chosen for Scorched Earth. The Aegis and the minion are being destroyed simultaneously. Does the Aegis have a chance to save the minion before it's destroyed?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If I target Bedrock with Scorched Earth, the Bedrock obviously isn't destroyed, but is everything else still destroyed?

a.canon: Yes. (Remember Avatars cannot be destroyed.)

q.canon: Can I choose zero sites?

a.canon: Yes. 'Any number' includes zero.

q.canon: If Scourge Zombies and an allied mortal die at the same time (e.g. Minor Explosion), does the Zombie's ability bring it back immediately?

a.canon: No, since the Scourge Zombies must be in the cemetery for their ability to trigger when the mortal dies.

q.canon: Who decides where the minion steps?

a.canon: The controller of Screamer.

q.canon: Is this forced movement?

a.canon: No, the enemy is taking their own step which can benefit from movement abilities such as Voidwalk or Airborne.

q.canon: If Sea Raider attacks a 3 power minion, killing it but also dying in the process, does the Raider have time to use their ability before they die?

a.canon: Yes. After units are killed, there is time for effects to resolve (e.g. Deathrite) before minions are placed in cemeteries. This effect resolves in the same window of time as deathrites.

q.canon: If I declare an attack against one target, but then a different enemy defends, does that satisfy this ability?

a.canon: Yes. An attack was made, and then a minion was killed. As long as your attacking unit used the Move and Attack ability and then got kill credit, this ability is satisfied.

q.canon: Does this actually target the Avatar?

a.canon: Yes. If your opponent casts this and targets your Warded avatar, you will not draw any cards and the Ward will break. Normal targeting rules apply (e.g. a spellcaster in the void or subsurface couldn't target an avatar with this magic, since they aren't in the same region).

q.canon: How does this interact with damage prevention effects?

a.canon: Damage prevention effects on the avatar will still apply to the damage from Searing Truth.

q.canon: What do X cost spells count as for this effect?

a.canon: Unless resolving on the storyline, X cost spells are treated as costing zero.

q.canon: If my avatar is nearby Seasoned Sellsword, can I discard a card for her ability even if I already control her?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: How can I kill a Hydra?

a.canon: Deal 1 lethal damage, or 6 damage all at once. Multiple sources of simultaneous damage will work. For example, if the Hydra attacks and two Bosk Trolls defend, the Hydra will be killed. Note that damage done one at a time, e.g. Arcane Barrage, would not kill it, since each individual 1 damage would be immediately healed.

q.canon: If it tries to become a basic copy of an aura animated by Enchantress, what happens?

a.canon: Selfsame Simulacrum becomes an aura (not a minion), since that's the actual text on the animated aura. As soon as Selfsame Simulacrum is an aura, it expands to its proper size based on card text (and default aura rules), and must continue to occupy the location that was specified during casting.

q.canon: Can it enter the realm Submerged if it copies a Submerged minion (or Voidwalk, or Burrowing)?

a.canon: No. When you cast a minion spell, you specify where the minion will enter the realm at time of casting. When the minion actually enters the realm (i.e. it's summoned), that's when Selfsame Simulacrum's copy ability applies. Without Submerge / Burrowing / Voidwalk when it's cast, Selfsame Simulacrum can't use those abilities to change where it's summoned.

q.canon: Does it copy Genesis abilities?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: What if it loses its abilities (e.g. Silence aura)?

a.canon: Selfsame Simulacrum remains a copy, but any abilities that were printed on the original copy are now ignored.

q.canon: How is the facing for the Trap determined?

a.canon: When you conjure the Sentinel Trap into the realm, choose a cardinal direction to be its initial facing. It then rotates from there. If it is teleported, the controller of the teleport effect can choose which cardinal direction it ends up facing.

q.canon: What happens if the Trap is animated?

a.canon: The direction it is facing is tracked normally, and is not affected by the Trap's movement or actions.

q.canon: Does the Spellcaster have to be a unit to tap and release the Demon?

a.canon: Yes. Only units can tap, so a spellcaster artifact or site would be unable to release the demon.

q.canon: My Shield Maidens attack, and then 3 Foot Soldiers defend. How much damage do my Shield Maidens take?

a.canon: 0, because each source of damage is reduced by 1!

q.canon: Can this target sub-surface minions?

a.canon: Yes. The minion must be nearby to the site, which means it must be near one of the site's locations. This means that minions which are underground (or underwater, if the Shrike Orchard is flooded) can be targeted by this effect.

q.canon: Do both units need to have been in play for a turn or have charge?

a.canon: Yes. Summoning sick units can't be tapped to pay costs.

q.canon: What happens if a Mountain Giant occupies a Silence aura?

a.canon: A card's size is generally set when it enters the realm, and is considered one of its characteristics, not an ability. It will not resize.

q.canon: What happens if a Silence aura is animated by Enchantress?

a.canon: It still silences other minions but it also silences itself.

q.canon: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: How do I calculate the difference in cost of the two minions?

a.canon: Start with the cost of the Evil minion in your hand, then subtract the cost of the Mortal at the Pond. Remember that costs cannot be negative, so if the result is below zero, treat it as zero instead.

q.canon: Can I transform a Mortal I do not control into Evil from my hand?

a.canon: Yes, though since it is a transform effect, control of the transformed minion will not change. The player who controlled the Mortal will control the Evil that came from your hand.

q.canon: Can my opponent use this effect as well?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: Can enemy projectiles be shot from Morien's location?

a.canon: No, Morien cuts them down immediately, like the total badass he is.

q.canon: If my opponent's beast snatches Tom up, do they now take control of him?

a.canon: How dare you!? Sir Tom Thumb is no mere trinket. He's a fully autonomous being and acknowledges no other controller!

q.canon: If Deathspeaker uses his ability to cast Skeleton Mage, does the Skeleton Mage get to use its genesis ability (casting and resolving a spell) before being banished?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: How does this ability work?

a.canon: After declaring their movement path but before actually moving, Skirmishers may shoot. (The game will lookahead to see if your declared path will actually result in movement, ignoring all triggered abilities but considering all ongoing effects.) Alternately, Skirmishers may shoot when they enter a new location during basic movement. They get one shot total during their basic movement, regardless of how far they move. Note that basic movement includes movement from a basic ability, i.e. Move and Attack, and Defend.

q.canon: Is this an activated ability that I use while Slimy Mutants are in my hand?

a.canon: Yes! While Slimy Mutants are in your hand, you may pay (3) and resolve the effect.

q.canon: If attacked by a minion that strikes first, does the Giantess end up striking back?

a.canon: Yes, assuming she isn't killed.

q.canon: What happens if there are two Smokestacks of Gnaak nearby each other?

a.canon: See 'Example - Two Smokestacks of Gnaak' in the codex!

q.canon: How do Smokestacks of Gnaak and Mirror Realm interact?

a.canon: By the time Mirror Realm enters the realm, it's already a copy. Thus, it can copy a nearby site, and then promptly loses all abilities of that copied site (but still is the copy, without abilities). See 'Apply Ongoing Effects In Order' in the codex for nitty-gritty details.

q.canon: How do Smokestacks of Gnaak and Rift Valley interact?

a.canon: Rift Valley enters the realm using its ability, and only loses its ability once it's in the realm (which by then, it doesn't really matter).

q.canon: Are minions along the path affected even if they have stealth?

a.canon: Yes! Projectiles do not hit stealth minions, but Snowball is just using the projectile to draw a path. It doesn't matter what units are hit, all of them along the path are rolled up in the snowball and pulled along!

q.canon: Does the snowball's path include both the starting and ending locations?

a.canon: Yes! The projectile's path determines which locations are affected by the rest of the snowball, gathering up everything along the way, just as you'd expect giant snowball physics would work after watching all those Saturday morning cartoons.

q.canon: If I happen to play a Lone Tower from the top of my atlas, will the mana from the Genesis ability also be doubled? What about mana from Abundance?

a.canon: Yes. Any mana that the site produces, including via any abilities, will be doubled.

q.canon: Can any of my spellcasters cast a spell and still benefit from my avatar's ability?

a.canon: Yes! As long as you control the spellcaster, the game sees it as a spell 'you' cast, meaning the player.

q.canon: Is the damage considered air damage?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: If I give my Sparkmage a poisonous dagger, will it deal lethal damage with its tap ability?

a.canon: Yes, because it's dealing the damage directly via it's ability. (Damage from a lightning bolt cast by the Sparkmage would not be lethal.)

q.canon: If I reduce the threshold required to cast the spell (e.g. Mix Aer), does the threshold still count for the Sparkmage ability?

a.canon: Yes. The Sparkmage ability considers printed threshold on the spell.

q.canon: What if the minion being killed occupies more than one location?

a.canon: You choose where the spear teleports, which will be a single location the minion occupies.

q.canon: What does 'Avatars here can't leave' mean?

a.canon: Avatars currently under the Sphere of Animosity can't enter locations not occupied by the Sphere. This means they can't move to those locations, or be moved by force. Note that when a site moves, it carries along cards of normal size with it, and those cards do not count as entering a new location. This means that a moving site can carry an Avatar out of the Sphere.

q.canon: Does this card count as an 'attack' since it has the word 'attack' in its name?

a.canon: Sorry for the confusion, but no, this is not actually an attack! You only get an 'attack' from the Move and Attack basic ability, or card text that specifically uses the word attack (e.g. Crave Golem). This card text uses the word 'strike,' which means the unit simply deals damage equal to its power (and there's no chance for the opponent to Defend, and you can strike Stealthed or Airborne units, etc.)

q.canon: Does Spire satisfy the Spire Lich?

a.canon: Yes, because of the golden rule. Be cool!

q.canon: Does Watchtower satisfy the Spire Lich?

a.canon: Yes, because of the golden rule. Be cool!

q.canon: When is the power of the minion checked to see if it's small enough to summon to any site?

a.canon: You check at the time of casting, before the minion enters the realm. This means that you can summon a Vengeful Heir to any site, even if it enters the realm as a minion which would be too large to work with Spore Sprouts normally, for example.

q.canon: Let's say the Mass is 1 power, and it fights another 1 power minion. What happens?

a.canon: Both take 1 damage each, which results in their simultaneous death. That triggers Squirming Mass's ability, which means its gains +1 power, but it's already dying, and merely gaining power isn't enough to save it. (Something specifically that saves a unit from death would be necessary, like Gilded Aegis.) In this example, both minions are placed in the cemetery.

q.canon: If a minion's current power is different from its printed power when it dies, which value does Squirming Mass gain?

a.canon: The current power of the minion that dies.

q.canon: Can this Pick Up and carry enemy minions?

a.canon: Yes, the coach will carry anyone!

q.canon: How does this ability work?

a.canon: The Abomination takes damage as if it is one unit, but the player causing the damage can choose which part or parts of the Abomination it applies to (after damage reduction, if any). Once a part has enough damage assigned to kill it, it's removed. When the last part of the Abomination is destroyed, so is the Abomination. For example, I have an Abomination with 5 + 4 + 3 power, and you are dealing it 7 damage from a Major Explosion. You can assign 3 and 4 damage, destroying those parts, and it's left with 5 power. Alternately, if it were my own Major Explosion, I could assign 3 damage to the 5-power part, and 3 damage to the 4-power part, and 1 damage to 3-power part. It's left with 5+4+3 power, with some damage on each of those parts (which will be removed normally at end of turn). If an effect would destroy or kill the Abomination outright, including taking Lethal damage, all of its parts are killed. If an effect would banish the Abomination, all of it is banished.

q.canon: When does this ability resolve?

a.canon: Whenever an enemy announces a Magic spell, after they've paid the costs but before the spell resolves.

q.canon: What does 'closer' mean?

a.canon: Determine which location it could step to using its normal movement that would be closest to the caster that triggered it. For instance, assume the Sturmgeist is at location S, and the spellcaster is at location C: Because the Sturmgeist has the airborne ability, it is able to get from S to C in one step, so it must do so, leaving it zero steps away from the caster. It cannot move to A or B, because those locations are still one step away from the caster, which is further than zero steps.

q.canon: If the spellcaster dies before the spell they cast resolves, will their spell still resolve?

a.canon: No! If the spellcaster is dead before their spell resolves, the spell will not resolve at all. See 'Source is No Longer in the Realm' for more details.

links.name: Source is No Longer in the Realm

q.canon: What if the Magic is cast by something other than a unit?

a.canon: The Sturmgeist only hears spells cast by enemies, which are units. Spells cast by artifacts (e.g. Omphalos) or sites (e.g. River of Flame) will not trigger its ability.

q.canon: Does this allow me to summon my units burrowed even without burrowing?

a.canon: No. The effect only allows you to break the restriction of choosing one of your own sites, but not the rule about summoning atop the site.

q.canon: The term 'summon' means 'enter the realm.' So, does that mean I can play minions here for free?

a.canon: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon your minions.

q.canon: Do I get the cards immediately when my minion carrying the treasure moves to the surface, even in the middle of something else (like defending or attacking) ?

a.canon: Yes! As soon as your unit is on the surface, you resolve the treasure effect.

q.canon: If one target is a minion, can the other target be an artifact, and vice versa?

a.canon: Yes. Target one (minion or artifact) and target another (minion or artifact).

q.canon: How exactly do I resolve a 'swap' effect?

a.canon: The two cards are simultaneously teleported to each other's location. If one of the targets cannot be targeted or teleported (e.g. Iron Man Talus), neither target moves.

q.canon: Can this effect swap cards into different regions?

a.canon: No. You target both cards being swapped, and targets must be in the same region as the caster. See Casting Spells for more information.

q.canon: What if one or both of the swapped cards were being carried?

a.canon: If either card was being carried by a unit, that unit will be carrying the newly swapped artifact/minion, due to the golden rule. For example, if two carried artifacts are swapped, the bearers will be carrying their newly swapped artifacts (even if they both are in the same location). If a minion is swapped with an artifact, presumably the minion will be immediately dropped (unless the new bearer can carry minions) and the artifact will not be carried (unless the swapped minion was being carried before it was swapped).

q.canon: What if an oversized unit is involved?

a.canon: Choose one of the locations the oversized unit occupies as the destination of the other card. See 'Teleporting Oversized Units' for more details.

q.canon: How do I resolve this effect if I sacrifice a card that has multiple types (e.g. Automaton) ?

a.canon: When you sacrifice a card that has multiple types, you may specify which type your opponent must match. For example, if you sacrifice one automaton (Minion and Artifact), you can force your opponent to sacrifice a minion or an artifact, your choice (not both). Similarly, if you're playing as Enchantress and you sacrifice an animated aura (Minion and Aura), you can force your opponent to sacrifice a minion or an aura, your choice (not both).

q.canon: What is the timing for the resolution of this spell?

a.canon: Choose an ally, declare its movement steps, placing them on the Storyline, then resolve those steps. Repeat for each ally. That is, you declare and resolve each ally's steps before proceeding to the next ally. If you gain more allies during the resolution, you may move them too; keep repeating the effect until each ally has moved.

q.canon: Can any of my spellcasters cast a spell and still benefit from my avatar's ability?

a.canon: Yes! As long as you control the spellcaster, the game sees it as a spell 'you' cast, meaning the player.

q.canon: Once the Thankless Squire has delivered all those lances, and isn't carrying any more, is it still Immobile?

a.canon: Yes, he's very tired and in need of a rest.

q.canon: What does it mean to 'build The Tower of Babel' and 'play ... atop this' ?

a.canon: You may play The Apex of Babel onto the same square as The Base of Babel! (If you have multiple copes of The Base of Babel in the realm, choose one.) If you do, they merge into a single site called The Tower of Babel. When you build it by playing the Apex, resolve the effect on The Apex of Babel. The Tower of Babel is considered a single site that provides (2) mana and (A)(E), and is both Unique and Exceptional. (The turn you play it, you gain (1) more mana since the Base was already in play.) If it's destroyed, both The Apex of Babel and The Base of Babel go to your cemetery. If it's copied, e.g. Mirror Realm, the copy will provide (2) mana, etc., but you won't get the build bonus again. For all purposes, The Tower of Babel is considered a single site.

q.canon: What does it mean to 'build The Tower of Babel' and 'play ... atop this' ?

a.canon: You may play The Apex of Babel onto the same square as The Base of Babel! (If you have multiple copes of The Base of Babel in the realm, choose one.) If you do, they merge into a single site called The Tower of Babel. When you build it by playing the Apex, resolve the effect on The Apex of Babel. The Tower of Babel is considered a single site that provides (2) mana and (A)(E), and is both Unique and Exceptional. (The turn you play it, you gain (1) more mana since the Base was already in play.) If it's destroyed, both The Apex of Babel and The Base of Babel go to your cemetery. If it's copied, e.g. Mirror Realm, the copy will provide (2) mana, etc., but you won't get the build bonus again. For all purposes, The Tower of Babel is considered a single site.

q.canon: If it's not adjacent to void and is within Abundance, does it still gain extra mana?

a.canon: Yes. The site doesn't provide mana normally, but if it's modified in some way (e.g. Abundance), then it can provide additional mana. 0 + 1 = 1.

q.canon: If it's not adjacent to void and is the target of a flood, does it still gain water affinity?

a.canon: Yes. The site doesn't provide affinity normally, but if it's modified in some way (e.g. Flood), then it will.

q.canon: Can this minion die?

a.canon: The only way it can be killed is if you sacrifice it. Otherwise, it cannot be killed. Meet your doom!

q.canon: If Draconian Bonekite, Sir Pelleas, and Azuridge Caravan are all in the realm, can I choose to keep the Caravan and another minion?

a.canon: No, you cannot save Azuridge Caravan and other minions. Since Azuridge Caravan counts as all minion types, you cannot save it and any other minion with a type since they will always have a shared type.

q.canon: If there are minions with multiple types in the realm, can I choose what type they count as when resolving The Flood? (e.g. I control Draconian Bonekite and Wyvern.

a.canon: They are both of their minion types at all times. Though each minion has another minion type in addition to Dragon in their type line, you can only choose one! You can only save one Dragon from the flood!

q.canon: Who chooses what minions of each type are saved from The Flood?

a.canon: The controller of the spell.

q.canon: Can I choose to save a minion that has no minion type e.g. Maiden, Mother, Crone?

a.canon: No, since Maiden, Mother, Crone has no type it cannot be saved from being submerged.

q.canon: If multiple minions including Miracle Workers die at the same time on Geistwood, can Miracle Workers return themselves and/or another minion that's dying to your hand?

a.canon: No, because Miracle Workers only return minions from the cemetery, and deathrites resolve while the minions are still in the realm. The Miracle Workers could return other minions that died earlier that turn and were in the cemetery.

q.canon: If The Geistwood site itself and minions occupying the site are all destroyed at the same time, do the minions' genesis abilities still count as Deathrite abilities, or can the active player decide to destroy Geistwood before the deathrites resolve?

a.canon: Since the destruction is simultaneous (e.g. Roots of Ygdrassil), all Deathrites will resolve before cards are moved to the cemetery.

q.canon: How does summoning burrowed interact with Evil Presence?

a.canon: You may summon the Haunts to an affected site, and they must be burrowed. But the Haunts won't gain Charge and Evil Presence will remain in the realm because the Haunts were not summoned 'here' according to Evil Presence, since Evil Presence occupies the surface (and perhaps the void), not underground.

q.canon: What does 'alone here' mean?

a.canon: No other units at the location.

q.canon: What counts as 'playing' a card?

a.canon: Playing a site, which costs 0, or casting a spell.

q.canon: If I modify the cost of a spell (e.g. a Mix artifact, or an alternate casting cost), does The Immortal Throne look at the modified cost or the printed cost?

a.canon: Cost in this case means 'printed cost.'

q.canon: The alpha foil version has the text for Pendulum of Peril on it. Is that a misprint?

a.canon: Yes. Use the text for the normal version. The foil version is not legal for tournament play.

q.canon: What happens if my opponent searches my spellbook but doesn't see this card when searching?

a.canon: If it's in your spellbook and they could see it, The Inquisition will trigger and be summoned! Tell your opponent that the card is in your spellbook and reveal it to them. If your opponent is only searching a limited part of your spellbook (e.g. Haystack), The Inquisition will only trigger if it was in the part of your spellbook that was actually searched. If there's a question, a judge can verify that The Inquisition wasn't there.

q.canon: When does this ability trigger?

a.canon: If an effect requires you to reveal it from your hand, or from your spellbook, or if your opponent searches your spellbook.

q.canon: What happens if I name this card when playing Feast for Crows?

a.canon: You would complete the search effect and banish The Inquisition before it triggers. Turns out sometimes you do expect them.

q.canon: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: If the 3 damage is reduced, redirected away from 'here', or prevented, do I still heal 3?

a.canon: No, the full 3 damage must be dealt to the targeted minion here in order to heal 3.

q.canon: Stretch my avatar? You're pulling my leg! Does this make my avatar an oversized unit now?

a.canon: Pulling both arms and both legs actually but, yes! Your avatar will now be an oversized unit!

q.canon: If Magellan Globe leaves play when a card is spanning the edge of the realm, what happens?

a.canon: Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for a minion, it dies. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for an avatar, shrink it until there is a legal position (Avatar controller's choice), and place it there.

q.canon: When an avatar is stretched by this effect, does it count as entering the new location?

a.canon: Yes! The avatar has to be able to enter the location for the effect to work, and then it will trigger any effects caused by entering. It does not count as moving, however.

q.canon: What happens if an oversized avatar is occupying a site, and then some effect moves that site?

a.canon: When a site moves, only things of 'normal' size move with it. As the avatar is now oversized, it will not be moved. In most cases when a site moves, another site will be left in its place (e.g. Rift Valley). In these situations, the avatar will end up occupying the surface of the new site. In the case of Cloud City, which leaves a void location behind, the avatar will now be occupying that void square. See mandatory actions for what happens if your avatar is in the void. Note that in both cases the avatar does not 'enter' the new location that it is occupying.

q.canon: How does this site work?

a.canon: The site still has both a surface and subsurface, but those locations also count as void simultaneously. It has a surface + void location, and a subsurface + void location. Minions without voidwalk that enter the site will be banished. Spells cast from the surface + void location can target cards that are in the surface or the void, for example. Projectiles can travel from the surface + void location into the void.

q.canon: Can my avatar enter this site?

a.canon: Yes.

q.canon: Can forced movement move a minion from a surface location to the surface of The Void?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: When my opponent casts a minion spell with Voidwalk, can they choose The Void as its summoning location, even though it's my site?

a.canon: Yes! It is a void, so they can choose to cast their Voidwalk minions to here if they wish.

q.canon: While my Avatar occupies the surface + void location of The Void site, can I target something occupying the underground + void location of The Void site?

a.canon: Yes! The target is in the same region (void) as the spellcaster, so it can be targeted!

q.canon: Normally, when moving from void to a site, a minion (e.g. Hounds of Ondaros) can move directly to the surface OR subsurface. Therefore, when moving from the subsurface + void location of this site, can a minion like Hounds of Ondaros move directly to the surface of an adjacent site? Could they move from the surface + void location directly to the subsurface of an adjacent site?

a.canon: Yes! Minions with voidwalk can continue to use their voidwalk abilities to move accordingly.

q.canon: What does 'can't be targeted or damaged by magic' mean?

a.canon: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

q.canon: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?

a.canon: The beta text is correct.

q.canon: Can Tide Naiads move from an underwater location to an underground location?

a.canon: No. They would need to enter the underground location to flood it, and they cannot enter underground locations without burrowing.

q.canon: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?

a.canon: Yes!

q.canon: Must spells cast by the Omphalos match its elements?

a.canon: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

q.canon: How does this work with end of turn and damage clearing?

a.canon: The intent is that a 1 power minion with 1 damage + the Trinket would survive the turn.

q.canon: Do I have to reveal the traded artifacts?

a.canon: Yes, you must reveal them to ensure it is a fair trade.

q.canon: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?

a.canon: The beta text is correct.

q.canon: What is a 'lone enemy'?

a.canon: A 'lone enemy' is an enemy unit that's not entering simultaneously with another enemy unit. Stationary units at the Troll Bridge ignored. Here are some examples: If an enemy War Horse is carrying its Avatar and moves to your Troll Bridge, it will not trigger, since there are two enemies entering simultaneously. If your Bodach Bogeyman is carrying two enemy minions and moves to your Troll Bridge, it will not trigger. However, if the Bogeyman were carrying just one enemy, the Bridge would trigger. If there is already an enemy occupying the Troll Bridge and another enemy unit enters, it will trigger for the entering enemy.

q.canon: In limited play (i.e. Sealed and Draft), may I cast Serava Townsfolk and Eltham Townsfolk from outside my card pool?

a.canon: Yes! Those cards have 'Townsfolk' in their name, and are thus covered by the 'specifically named card' rule for limited games. You do not need them in your collection in draft or sealed. You still need to meet the threshold requirement to cast them, though!
